apiChange.author: kerthcet
apiChange.userFacingChange: Introduce NodeInclusionPolicies to specify nodeAffinity/nodeTaint strategy when calculating pod topology spread skew.

enrichment.problem: TopologySpreadConstraints could not specify how nodeAffinity or nodeTaints should be considered when the scheduler calculates pod skew, leading to unpredictable or sub‑optimal pod distribution across nodes.
enrichment.affected: Any workload that uses `TopologySpreadConstraints` and node affinity or tolerations, such as Deployments, StatefulSets, or custom controllers that depend on even pod distribution.
enrichment.fix: Added a new `NodeInclusionPolicy` field to `TopologySpreadConstraints` in the PodSpec, allowing users to define the nodeAffinity/nodeTaint strategy (e.g., honor or ignore) that the scheduler uses when computing topology spread skew.
enrichment.impact: Provides precise control over pod placement and spread calculations, enabling more reliable traffic distribution and reducing unintended skew, especially for workloads that rely on specific node affinity or tolerations.

apiChange.description:
Introduced NodeIPAM support for multiple ClusterCIDRs ([#2593](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/2593)) as an alpha feature.
Set feature gate `MultiCIDRRangeAllocator=true`, determines whether the `MultiCIDRRangeAllocator` controller can be used, while the kube-controller-manager flag below will pick the active controller.
Enabled the `MultiCIDRRangeAllocator` by setting `--cidr-allocator-type=MultiCIDRRangeAllocator` flag in kube-controller-manager.
apiChange.author: sarveshr7
apiChange.userFacingChange:
NodeIPAM support for multiple ClusterCIDRs (https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/2593) introduced as an alpha feature.

Setting feature gate MultiCIDRRangeAllocator=true, determines whether the MultiCIDRRangeAllocator controller can be used, while the kube-controller-manager flag below will pick the active controller.

Enable the MultiCIDRRangeAllocator by setting --cidr-allocator-type=MultiCIDRRangeAllocator flag in kube-controller-manager.

enrichment.problem: Clusters could only allocate pod IPs from a single ClusterCIDR, preventing use of multiple CIDR ranges (e.g., dual‑stack or multi‑network setups).
enrichment.affected: Clusters that need multiple CIDR ranges for pod IP allocation, such as dual‑stack or multi‑network deployments.
enrichment.fix: Adds an alpha NodeIPAM implementation that supports multiple ClusterCIDRs via the MultiCIDRRangeAllocator controller. Enable with the MultiCIDRRangeAllocator feature gate and the `--cidr-allocator-type=MultiCIDRRangeAllocator` flag in kube‑controller‑manager.
enrichment.impact: Clusters can now allocate pod IPs from several CIDR ranges, enabling dual‑stack clusters and more flexible network designs without custom solutions.

apiChange.description: The `metadata.clusterName` field is completely removed. This should not have any user-visible impact.
apiChange.author: lavalamp

enrichment.problem: The `metadata.clusterName` field was removed from the Kubernetes API schema.
enrichment.affected: Any component or custom code that accessed `metadata.clusterName` directly will no longer find the field, though typical users and workloads are not affected.
enrichment.fix: The change deletes the `metadata.clusterName` field from all API objects, cleaning up the API and related code paths.
enrichment.impact: No user‑visible impact; existing workloads and tools will not see the field, and normal cluster operation is unchanged.

apiChange.description: Support for the alpha seccomp annotations `seccomp.security.alpha.kubernetes.io/pod` and `container.seccomp.security.alpha.kubernetes.io`, deprecated since v1.19, was partially removed. Kubelets no longer support the annotations, use of the annotations in static pods is no longer supported, and the seccomp annotations are no longer auto-populated when pods with seccomp fields are created. Auto-population of the seccomp fields from the annotations is planned to be removed in 1.27. Pods  should use the corresponding pod or container `securityContext.seccompProfile` field instead.
apiChange.author: saschagrunert
apiChange.userFacingChange: Action required: support for the alpha seccomp annotations `seccomp.security.alpha.kubernetes.io/pod` and `container.seccomp.security.alpha.kubernetes.io`, deprecated since v1.19, has been partially removed. Kubelets no longer support the annotations, use of the annotations in static pods is no longer supported, and the seccomp annotations are no longer auto-populated when pods with seccomp fields are created. Auto-population of the seccomp fields from the annotations is planned to be removed in 1.27. Pods should use the corresponding pod or container `securityContext.seccompProfile` field instead.

issueContext.title: Remove version skew and annotation support for seccomp (v1.23)
issueContext.body:
This is a placeholder issue to remove support for the version skew handling as well as the deprecated seccomp annotations.

The [KEP](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/master/keps/sig-node/20190717-seccomp-ga.md) states:

> Since we support up to 2 minor releases of version skew between the master and node, annotations must continue to be supported and backfilled for at least 2 versions passed the initial implementation. However, we can decide to extend support farther to reduce breakage. If this feature is implemented in v1.19, I propose v1.23 as a target for removal of the old behavior.
…
> To raise awareness of annotation usage (in case of old automation), a warning mechanism will be used to highlight that support will be dropped in v1.23. The mechanisms being considerated are audit annotations, annotations on the object, events, or a warning as described in KEP #1693.

Beside that, the kubelet `--seccomp-profile-root` has to be removed in v1.23, too:

> The existing kubelet (alpha) flag --seccomp-profile-root allows for seccomp root path configuration. This flag will be deprecated as of v1.19, and will be removed on v1.23. The seccomp root path will then be derived from the kubelet root path, which is defined by --root-dir. The current default value is <root-dir>/seccomp. This KEP will make the default behavior the only behavior.


/milestone v1.23
/sig node

cc @tallclair @pjbgf

enrichment.problem: The alpha seccomp annotations `seccomp.security.alpha.kubernetes.io/pod` and `container.seccomp.security.alpha.kubernetes.io` were deprecated in v1.19, but Kubelet still accepted them. In this release the support is partially removed: Kubelet no longer recognises these annotations, static pods cannot use them, and they are no longer auto‑populated into the `securityContext.seccompProfile` fields.
enrichment.affected: Pods that use the alpha seccomp annotations, especially static pods and clusters that still rely on annotation‑based Seccomp configuration.
enrichment.fix: Kubelet now ignores the deprecated annotations. Pods must explicitly set the Seccomp profile using the stable `securityContext.seccompProfile` field at the pod or container level. The auto‑population behavior will be fully removed in v1.27.
enrichment.impact: Any workload that relied on the deprecated seccomp annotations (including static pods and automation that sets those annotations) will lose its Seccomp profile configuration and will run without the intended Seccomp restrictions until the spec is updated. Migrating to `securityContext.seccompProfile` restores the intended security posture.

apiChange.description:
There is a new OCI image registry (`registry.k8s.io`) that can be used to pull Kubernetes images. The old registry (`k8s.gcr.io`) will continue to be supported for the foreseeable future, but the new name should perform better because it frontends equivalent mirrors in other clouds.  Please point your clusters to the new registry going forward. 

Admission/Policy integrations that have an allowlist of registries need to include `registry.k8s.io` alongside `k8s.gcr.io`.
Air-gapped environments and image garbage-collection configurations will need to update to pre-pull and preserve required images under `registry.k8s.io` as well as `k8s.gcr.io`.
apiChange.author: dims
apiChange.userFacingChange:
There is a new OCI image registry (registry.k8s.io) that can be used to pull kubernetes images. The old registry (k8s.gcr.io) will continue to be supported for the foreseeable future, but the new name should perform better because it frontends equivalent mirrors in other clouds.  Please point your clusters to the new registry going forward. 

Action Required: Admission/Policy integrations that have an allowlist of registries need to include "registry.k8s.io" alongside "k8s.gcr.io".
Action Required: Air-gapped environments and image garbage-collection configurations will need to update to pre-pull and preserve required images under "registry.k8s.io" as well as "k8s.gcr.io".

enrichment.problem: Clusters and tooling still reference the historic image registry k8s.gcr.io, but a new OCI registry (registry.k8s.io) is now recommended. Admission/Policy allowlists, air‑gapped pre‑pull scripts, and image garbage‑collection configs that only include k8s.gcr.io will miss required images, leading to pull failures or unintended GC.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes clusters that pull component images, administrators configuring image allowlists, air‑gapped environments, and any tooling that performs image garbage collection or pre‑pulling.
enrichment.fix: Introduce the new registry name registry.k8s.io as the preferred source for all Kubernetes component images. Update documentation and encourage users to point clusters to this registry. Policy allowlists must now include registry.k8s.io, and air‑gapped or GC configurations should pre‑pull and preserve images from both registries.
enrichment.impact: Using registry.k8s.io improves image download performance by routing through cloud‑native mirrors. Updating allowlists and pre‑pull/GC settings prevents image‑pull errors and ensures continuous operation of clusters, especially in restricted or air‑gapped environments.

apiChange.description: the `minDomains` field in Pod Topology Spread is graduated to beta
apiChange.author: sanposhiho

enrichment.problem: The `minDomains` field for Pod Topology Spread constraints was only available as an alpha feature, limiting its reliability and use in production environments.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using or planning to use Pod Topology Spread constraints that require a minimum domain count for pod placement.
enrichment.fix: Graduated the `minDomains` field to beta, making it a stable, supported part of the Pod Topology Spread API.
enrichment.impact: Users can now safely use `minDomains` to specify the minimum number of distinct topology domains a pod should be spread across, enabling more predictable pod placement and load balancing in production clusters.

apiChange.description: The `PodSecurity` admission plugin has graduated to GA and is enabled by default. The admission configuration version has been promoted to `pod-security.admission.config.k8s.io/v1`.
apiChange.author: wangyysde
apiChange.userFacingChange: The PodSecurity admission plugin has graduated to GA and is enabled by default. The admission configuration version has been promoted to `pod-security.admission.config.k8s.io/v1`.

issueContext.title: [PodSecurity] Add v1 config API (pod-security.admission.config.k8s.io)
issueContext.body:
GA blocker (https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/2579)

/sig auth
/milestone v1.25
/help

enrichment.problem: The PodSecurity admission plugin was only available as a beta feature and required manual enablement and a beta version of the admission configuration API, leading to inconsistent enforcement of pod security standards across clusters.
enrichment.affected: All clusters upgrading to the release and any workloads (pods) that are created without explicit pod‑security specifications will now be subject to the default policies.
enrichment.fix: The plugin has graduated to GA, is now enabled by default in the API server, and the admission configuration version has been promoted to pod-security.admission.config.k8s.io/v1, providing a stable, out‑of‑the‑box security enforcement mechanism.
enrichment.impact: Clusters get default pod security enforcement without extra configuration, and cluster operators can rely on a stable v1 API for defining pod security standards, improving security posture and reducing operational friction.

apiChange.description:
Kube-Scheduler ComponentConfig is graduated to GA, `kubescheduler.config.k8s.io/v1` is available now. 
Plugin `SelectorSpread` is removed in v1.
apiChange.author: kerthcet
apiChange.userFacingChange:
Kube-Scheduler ComponentConfig is graduated to GA, `kubescheduler.config.k8s.io/v1` is available now. 
Plugin `SelectorSpread` is removed in v1.

enrichment.problem: The kube-scheduler ComponentConfig was only available as a beta API and included the SelectorSpread plugin. Users configuring the scheduler with the beta version or relying on SelectorSpread may encounter incompatibilities after the upgrade.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that customize kube-scheduler via ComponentConfig, especially those using the beta API version or the SelectorSpread plugin.
enrichment.fix: The ComponentConfig is graduated to GA with the stable apiVersion `kubescheduler.config.k8s.io/v1`. The SelectorSpread plugin is removed from the v1 configuration, and validation now rejects its usage.
enrichment.impact: Clusters can now use a stable scheduler configuration API, improving reliability. Administrators must update any scheduler configs that reference the SelectorSpread plugin to alternative placement plugins, preventing config errors during upgrades.

apiChange.description:
The `endPort` field in Network Policy is now promoted to GA

Network Policy providers that support `endPort` field now can use it to specify a range of ports to apply a Network Policy.

Previously, each Network Policy could only target a single port.

Please be aware that `endPort` field MUST BE SUPPORTED by the Network Policy provider. In case your provider does not support `endPort` and this field is specified in a Network Policy, the Network Policy will be created covering only the port field (single port).
apiChange.author: rikatz
apiChange.userFacingChange:
endPort field in Network Policy is now promoted to GA

Network Policy providers that support endPort field now can use it to specify a range of ports to apply a Network Policy.

Previously, each Network Policy could only target a single port.

Please be aware that endPort field MUST BE SUPPORTED by the Network Policy provider. In case your provider does not support endPort and this field is specified in a Network Policy, the Network Policy will be created covering only the port field (single port).

enrichment.problem: NetworkPolicy could only target a single port, making it cumbersome to define policies that need a range of ports.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using NetworkPolicy to control traffic where port ranges are required, and CNI providers that implement NetworkPolicy enforcement.
enrichment.fix: The `endPort` field is promoted to GA; when a NetworkPolicy provider supports it, users can specify a port range (`port` to `endPort`) in a single policy.
enrichment.impact: Users can write simpler, more expressive NetworkPolicies for port ranges, reducing the number of policies needed and improving manageability. Providers must implement `endPort` support, otherwise only the single `port` is applied.

apiChange.description: Promote StatefulSet minReadySeconds to GA. This means `--feature-gates=StatefulSetMinReadySeconds=true` are not needed on kube-apiserver and kube-controller-manager binaries and they'll be removed soon following policy at https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/deprecation-policy/#deprecation
apiChange.author: ravisantoshgudimetla

enrichment.problem: StatefulSet `minReadySeconds` was a beta feature that required enabling the `StatefulSetMinReadySeconds` feature gate on the kube-apiserver and kube-controller-manager binaries. Users had to manage this flag manually, and the flag is slated for removal.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that use StatefulSet `minReadySeconds` and administrators who previously set the `StatefulSetMinReadySeconds` feature gate on kube-apiserver and kube-controller-manager.
enrichment.fix: The `minReadySeconds` field is promoted to GA, so the feature gate is no longer required. The `--feature-gates=StatefulSetMinReadySeconds=true` flag can be removed and will be deprecated in a future release.
enrichment.impact: Cluster operators no longer need to configure an extra feature gate for StatefulSets, simplifying deployment and reducing the risk of configuration drift. The change also prepares the removal of the obsolete flag, cleaning up the binary arguments.

apiChange.description:
Introduction of the `DisruptionTarget` pod condition type. Its `reason` field indicates the reason for pod termination:
- PreemptionByKubeScheduler (Pod preempted by kube-scheduler)
- DeletionByTaintManager (Pod deleted by taint manager due to NoExecute taint)
- EvictionByEvictionAPI (Pod evicted by Eviction API)
- DeletionByPodGC (an orphaned Pod deleted by PodGC)
apiChange.author: mimowo
apiChange.userFacingChange:
Introduction of the `DisruptionTarget` pod condition type. Its `reason` field indicates the reason for pod termination:
- PreemptionByKubeScheduler (Pod preempted by kube-scheduler)
- DeletionByTaintManager (Pod deleted by taint manager due to NoExecute taint)
- EvictionByEvictionAPI (Pod evicted by Eviction API)
- DeletionByPodGC (an orphaned Pod deleted by PodGC)

enrichment.problem: Users could not easily determine why a pod was terminated, making debugging and handling of pod disruptions ambiguous.
enrichment.affected: All workloads and operators that monitor pod status or need to react to pod termination events.
enrichment.fix: Added a new pod condition type `DisruptionTarget` with a `reason` field that surface the exact cause of termination (preemption, taint‑manager deletion, eviction API, or PodGC deletion).
enrichment.impact: Provides clear visibility into pod termination reasons, aiding troubleshooting, automation, and correct handling of retriable vs non‑retriable failures for workloads.

apiChange.description: Added alpha support for user namespaces in pods phase 1 (KEP 127, feature gate: UserNamespacesStatelessPodsSupport)
apiChange.author: rata

enrichment.problem: Pods could not run with user namespaces, limiting the ability to isolate container processes with distinct UID/GID mappings for security and compatibility purposes.
enrichment.affected: Cluster administrators and developers who need per‑pod UID/GID isolation on Linux nodes; workloads that benefit from user‑namespace based security isolation.
enrichment.fix: Introduced alpha support for pod user namespaces (phase 1) behind the UserNamespacesStatelessPodsSupport feature gate, enabling stateless pods to be created with user namespace mappings.
enrichment.impact: Allows clusters to begin using user namespace isolation for pods, improving security isolation and paving the way for future enhancements such as stateful pod support.

apiChange.description: Introduced support for handling pod failures with respect to the configured pod failure policy rules.
apiChange.author: mimowo
apiChange.userFacingChange: Introduces support for handling pod failures with respect to the configured pod failure policy rules

enrichment.problem: Jobs treated all pod failures identically because the podFailurePolicy rules were not enforced, causing unintended retries or premature job termination.
enrichment.affected: Jobs (and CronJobs) that specify a podFailurePolicy; any workload relying on that policy for failure handling.
enrichment.fix: Added support in the job controller to evaluate pod failures against the configured podFailurePolicy, handling retriable and non‑retriable failures according to the policy.
enrichment.impact: Allows users to reliably control job behavior on pod failures, reducing unnecessary restarts and improving workload stability.

apiChange.description: Added KMS v2alpha1 support.
apiChange.author: aramase

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes only supported the original KMS API version, so clusters could not use the newer KMS v2alpha1 interface for secret encryption, limiting compatibility with modern KMS providers.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that use envelope encryption for Secrets and wish to adopt KMS providers that only expose a v2alpha1 interface.
enrichment.fix: Introduces support for the KMS v2alpha1 API version, adding the necessary API objects, admission handling, and integration points so that the API server can use KMS v2alpha1 providers for envelope encryption.
enrichment.impact: Clusters can now configure and use KMS v2alpha1 providers, enabling newer encryption features and broader compatibility with external key management services without major configuration changes.

apiChange.description: Promoted DaemonSet MaxSurge to GA. This means `--feature-gates=DaemonSetUpdateSurge=true` are not needed on kube-apiserver and kube-controller-manager binaries and they'll be removed soon following policy at https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/deprecation-policy/#deprecation .
apiChange.author: ravisantoshgudimetla
apiChange.userFacingChange: Promote DaemonSet MaxSurge to GA. This means `--feature-gates=DaemonSetUpdateSurge=true` are not needed on kube-apiserver and kube-controller-manager binaries and they'll be removed soon following policy at https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/deprecation-policy/#deprecation

enrichment.problem: DaemonSet maxSurge functionality required the DaemonSetUpdateSurge feature gate to be enabled on kube-apiserver and kube-controller-manager binaries, adding configuration overhead and risking misconfiguration for users who wanted to use maxSurge.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that used DaemonSets and previously had to enable the DaemonSetUpdateSurge feature gate on kube-apiserver and kube-controller-manager binaries.
enrichment.fix: Promoted DaemonSet maxSurge to GA. The DaemonSetUpdateSurge feature gate is no longer needed; the functionality is always enabled and the flag will be removed in a future release.
enrichment.impact: Cluster operators no longer need to set or manage the DaemonSetUpdateSurge feature gate, simplifying cluster configuration and reducing the chance of upgrade‑time errors. Users can immediately use maxSurge in DaemonSet rolling updates with default GA stability guarantees.

apiChange.description: The Pod `spec.podOS` field is promoted to GA. The `IdentifyPodOS` feature gate unconditionally enabled, and will no longer be accepted as a `--feature-gates` parameter in 1.27.
apiChange.author: ravisantoshgudimetla

enrichment.problem: The IdentifyPodOS feature gate had to be enabled via the --feature-gates flag to use the pod.spec.podOS field. In 1.27 the gate is always on, and the flag is no longer accepted, causing upgrade failures for clusters that still include it.
enrichment.affected: Clusters upgrading to 1.27 that still specify IdentifyPodOS in --feature-gates, and any workloads that rely on the podOS field (especially Windows pods).
enrichment.fix: Promoted spec.podOS to GA, unconditionally enabled the IdentifyPodOS feature gate, and removed support for the flag in the apiserver command line.
enrichment.impact: Users can now set pod.spec.podOS (e.g., for Windows pods) without enabling a feature gate, simplifying configuration and preventing errors during upgrades when the flag is present.

apiChange.description: For v1.25, Kubernetes will be using golang 1.19, In this PR the version is updated to 1.19rc2 as GA is not yet available.
apiChange.author: dims
apiChange.userFacingChange: For v1.25, Kubernetes will be using golang 1.19, In this PR we update to 1.19rc2 as GA is not yet available.

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes v1.25 needed to be built with Go 1.19, but the official GA release of Go 1.19 was not yet available, requiring an interim RC version.
enrichment.affected: Developers and CI systems building Kubernetes v1.25; downstream projects that compile the source code.
enrichment.fix: Update the Kubernetes build configuration to use Go 1.19rc2 for v1.25 until the GA release becomes available.
enrichment.impact: Ensures that v1.25 can be compiled and released on schedule with the newer Go toolchain, maintaining compatibility and enabling use of Go 1.19 language/runtime improvements.

apiChange.description: The `CSIInlineVolume` feature has moved from beta to GA.
apiChange.author: dobsonj
apiChange.userFacingChange: The CSIInlineVolume feature has moved from beta to GA.

enrichment.problem: The CSIInlineVolume feature was only available as a beta feature, requiring the beta feature gate to be enabled and lacking GA stability guarantees.
enrichment.affected: Any cluster that uses or plans to use CSI inline volumes, especially those that previously needed to enable the CSIInlineVolume beta feature gate.
enrichment.fix: The feature has been graduated to GA: the beta feature gate is removed, the feature is enabled by default, and the APIs are marked stable.
enrichment.impact: Clusters can now use CSI inline volumes without enabling a feature gate, and users can rely on the stability and long‑term support of the feature. Existing workloads that already used the beta feature continue to work unchanged, while new deployments gain a stable storage option.

apiChange.description: Introduced PodHasNetwork condition for pods.
apiChange.author: ddebroy

enrichment.problem: There was no pod condition indicating whether a pod actually has an attached network, making it difficult for controllers, testing frameworks, and users to reliably detect network availability for a pod.
enrichment.affected: All pods in the cluster; any component or controller that reads pod conditions (e.g., testing frameworks, custom controllers) now has visibility into network availability.
enrichment.fix: Introduced a new Pod condition named `PodHasNetwork` that is set to true when a pod has an attached network and false otherwise.
enrichment.impact: Controllers, testing tools, and operators can now programmatically determine a pod's network status, improving handling of network‑dependent workloads, debugging, and test reliability.

issueContext.title: Promote Ephemeral Containers to GA
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

This issue tracks the change required to update the `EphemeralContainers` feature gate to GA

### Why is this needed?

This promotes ephemeral containers to GA

enrichment.problem: The EphemeralContainers feature was behind a feature gate that required users to manually enable it via the --feature-gates flag on kube-apiserver and kubelet. Continuing to set this flag after GA could cause confusion and future deprecation warnings.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that had explicitly enabled the EphemeralContainers feature gate in the kube-apiserver or kubelet command lines. Administrators need to update their static pod manifests or systemd service files to drop the flag.
enrichment.fix: EphemeralContainers is now generally available; the feature gate is permanently enabled. Users should remove the EphemeralContainers entry from the --feature-gates flag on both kube-apiserver and kubelet command lines.
enrichment.impact: Simplifies cluster configuration by eliminating the need to manage the EphemeralContainers feature gate and avoids future deprecation issues. Existing workloads can continue to use Ephemeral Containers without changes, and clusters become ready for upcoming removal of the flag.

apiChange.description: Promoted CronJob's TimeZone support to beta.
apiChange.author: soltysh
apiChange.userFacingChange: Promote CronJob's TimeZone support to beta

enrichment.problem: CronJob only had experimental (alpha) support for specifying a TimeZone, requiring a feature gate and lacking stability assurances.
enrichment.affected: Anyone creating CronJob objects who wants to schedule jobs based on a specific time zone.
enrichment.fix: Promoted the TimeZone field in CronJob spec to beta, enabling it by default and making the implementation stable and supported.
enrichment.impact: Users can now reliably schedule CronJobs using specific time zones without extra workarounds or feature‑gate flags, improving usability and reducing operational risk.

apiChange.description: The PodTopologySpread is respected after rolling upgrades.
apiChange.author: denkensk

issueContext.title: Rolling updates interfere with Pod Topology Spread Constraints
issueContext.body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->

**Background**:
We define Pod Topology Spread Constraints on our Deployment (labeled `app: app1`), as follows:
>       topologySpreadConstraints:
>       - maxSkew: 1
>         topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname
>         whenUnsatisfiable: DoNotSchedule
>         labelSelector:
>           matchLabels:
>             app: app1

The deployment is defined with 5 replicas.

**What happened**:
Triggering a rolling update on the running deployment will sometimes result in a skewed spread, not honoring the maxSkew=1.
Our theory is that the scheduler "sees" the old pods when deciding how to spread the new pods over nodes. When the old nodes are eventually terminated, we sometimes see three pods in node-1, two pods in node-2 and none in node-3.

**What you expected to happen**:
The maxSkew value in Pod Topology Spread Constraints should always be honored.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
It reproduces randomly, so it takes a few attempts until reproduced.
I'm running `kubectl rollout restart deployment <deployment-name>` a few times until it reproduces.

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): 1.19.7
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration: self deployed cluster with kubeadm on on-premises VMs (vmware)
- OS (e.g: `cat /etc/os-release`): CentOS 7
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`): 3.10.0-1160.6.1.el7.x86_64
- Other: cluster consists of 3 master nodes which also act as workers

issueContext.title: Topology spreading can become imbalanced during deployment rollout
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

When restarting a rolling deployment, the new pods can end up in imbalanced topologies that violate their specified `MaxSkew`. This is due to interference from the old, `Terminating` pods in the scheduler's topology size calculation. At scheduling time, the constraints are technically satisfied. However, once the old pods are removed, the topology size difference can be greater than `MaxSkew`

/sig scheduling

### What did you expect to happen?

Topology spread constraints should be valid during and after a deployment rollout

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Create a Kind cluster with the following config for 2 worker nodes:
```yaml
# three node (two workers) cluster config
kind: Cluster
apiVersion: kind.x-k8s.io/v1alpha4
nodes:
  - role: control-plane
  - role: worker
    kubeadmConfigPatches:
      - |
        kind: JoinConfiguration
        nodeRegistration:
          kubeletExtraArgs:
            node-labels: "topology.kubernetes.io/zone=A"
  - role: worker
    kubeadmConfigPatches:
      - |
        kind: JoinConfiguration
        nodeRegistration:
          kubeletExtraArgs:
            node-labels: "topology.kubernetes.io/zone=B"
```

Next, create a sample deployment to take up some cluster utilization (this may not be necessary)
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  labels:
    app: fat
  name: fat
  namespace: default
spec:
  replicas: 20
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: fat
  strategy:
    rollingUpdate:
      maxSurge: 25%
      maxUnavailable: 25%
    type: RollingUpdate
  template:
    metadata:
      creationTimestamp: null
      labels:
        app: fat
    spec:
      nodeSelector:
        kubernetes.io/hostname: "kind-worker2"
      containers:
        - command:
            - sh
            - -c
            - "trap : TERM INT; sleep 9999999999d & wait"
          image: alpine
          imagePullPolicy: Alway

enrichment.problem: During a rolling update of a Deployment, the scheduler considered terminating pods when calculating topology spread, leading to violations of the specified maxSkew in PodTopologySpread constraints. This caused uneven pod distribution across nodes after the old pods were terminated.
enrichment.affected: Workloads using Deployments (or other controllers) with PodTopologySpread constraints experience imbalanced pod placement during rolling updates.
enrichment.fix: The scheduler logic was updated to ignore terminating pods when evaluating PodTopologySpread constraints during rolling upgrades, ensuring that the maxSkew is always respected throughout and after the rollout.
enrichment.impact: Deployments that rely on PodTopologySpread for even pod placement will now maintain the desired distribution during rollouts, preventing node overload, improving reliability, and reducing the need for manual interventions.

apiChange.description: PersistentVolumeClaim objects are no longer left with storage class set to `nil` forever, but will be updated retroactively once any StorageClass is set or created as default.
apiChange.author: RomanBednar

enrichment.problem: PVCs created before any StorageClass existed were left with storageClassName set to nil and never updated, causing them to lack a storage class even after a default StorageClass is added.
enrichment.affected: Users with PersistentVolumeClaims that were created before any StorageClass existed, especially those relying on the default StorageClass for dynamic provisioning.
enrichment.fix: The PVC controller now retroactively patches PersistentVolumeClaim objects when a StorageClass is created or marked as default, assigning the appropriate storageClassName instead of leaving it nil.
enrichment.impact: PVCs will automatically receive the correct storage class, preventing pod startup failures and eliminating the need for manual PVC edits after a default StorageClass is introduced.

apiChange.description: Local Storage Capacity Isolation feature is GA in 1.25 release. For systems (rootless) that cannot check root file system, please use kubelet config --local-storage-capacity-isolation=false to disable this feature. Once disabled, pod cannot set local ephemeral storage request/limit, and emptyDir sizeLimit niether.
apiChange.author: jingxu97

enrichment.problem: Rootless kubelet instances cannot determine the capacity of the node's root filesystem, so the new Local Storage Capacity Isolation feature cannot operate correctly. The recommended workaround is to disable the feature with --local-storage-capacity-isolation=false, but when disabled pods are unable to set local ephemeral storage requests/limits or an emptyDir sizeLimit.
enrichment.affected: Users running rootless kubelet (e.g., kubelet inside containers) who rely on local storage capacity isolation for pod storage requests/limits.
enrichment.fix: The feature is now GA in v1.25. For rootless environments, users must explicitly disable it via the kubelet flag --local-storage-capacity-isolation=false. No additional code change is provided; this is the intended configuration path.
enrichment.impact: Clusters that run kubelet in rootless mode lose the ability to enforce storage requests and limits for local ephemeral storage and emptyDir sizeLimits, which can lead to unbounded local storage consumption on those nodes.

apiChange.description:
Extended ContainerStatus CRI API to allow runtime response with container resource requests and limits that are in effect.
- UpdateContainerResources CRI API now supports both Linux and Windows.
apiChange.author: vinaykul
apiChange.userFacingChange:
- Extends ContainerStatus CRI API to allow runtime response with container resource requests and limits that are in effect.
- UpdateContainerResources CRI API now supports both Linux and Windows.

For details, see KEPs below.

enrichment.problem: Prior to this change the ContainerStatus CRI response did not include the resource requests and limits actually applied to a container, and the UpdateContainerResources API was limited to Linux containers only. Users could not query or modify the effective resources of Windows containers, limiting in‑place resource updates and observability.
enrichment.affected: All workloads that need to read or modify container resource requests/limits, especially Windows pod workloads and any component that relies on accurate ContainerStatus information.
enrichment.fix: The ContainerStatus CRI API is extended to return the current resource requests and limits for each container. The UpdateContainerResources API is updated to accept and apply resource changes on both Linux and Windows containers.
enrichment.impact: Tools and controllers can now retrieve the exact resources a container is using and perform in‑place resource updates on Windows workloads, improving resource management, autoscaling decisions, and debugging of pod resource configurations.

other.description: The Go API for logging configuration in `k8s.io/component-base` was moved to `k8s.io/component-base/logs/api/v1`. The configuration file format and command line flags are the same as before.
other.author: pohly
other.userFacingChange: The Go API for logging configuration in k8s.io/component-base was moved to k8s.io/component-base/logs/api/v1. The configuration file format and command line flags are the same as before.

enrichment.problem: The Go logging configuration API was moved to a new package path (k8s.io/component-base/logs/api/v1), causing compile failures for code that imports the old path.
enrichment.affected: Go code (controllers, operators, or any component) that imports k8s.io/component-base for logging configuration.
enrichment.fix: The API definitions have been relocated to the new package. Existing configuration file format and command‑line flags remain unchanged; developers need to update import statements to the new path.
enrichment.impact: No change to cluster runtime behavior; only code that depends on the old import path must be recompiled with the new path. This is a straightforward source‑level migration.

other.description: The kube-controller-manager's deprecated `--experimental-cluster-signing-duration` flag is now removed. Adapt your machinery to use the `--cluster-signing-duration` flag that is available since v1.19.
other.author: ialidzhikov

enrichment.problem: The kube-controller-manager's deprecated `--experimental-cluster-signing-duration` flag has been removed, causing controller-manager startups that still reference this flag to fail or ignore the intended certificate signing duration.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that configure kube-controller-manager with the `--experimental-cluster-signing-duration` flag, typically via static pod manifests or custom deployments.
enrichment.fix: Update the controller-manager configuration (e.g., static pod manifest, systemd unit, or deployment) to use the supported `--cluster-signing-duration` flag introduced in v1.19.
enrichment.impact: Ensures the certificate signing controller continues to function correctly; prevents controller-manager crashes or misconfiguration that could disrupt automated certificate renewal across the cluster.

other.description: Added a deprecated warning for node beta label usage in PV/SC/RC and CSI Storage Capacity.
other.author: pacoxu
other.userFacingChange: add a deprecated warning for node beta label usage in pv/sc/rc and csi storage capacity

enrichment.problem: Users can still set the legacy node beta label (node.beta.kubernetes.io/...) on PersistentVolumes, StorageClasses, ReplicationControllers, and CSI StorageCapacity objects, which is deprecated and will be removed in a future release, leading to potential future failures.
enrichment.affected: Any workloads or administrators that rely on the node beta label in PV, StorageClass, RC, or CSI Storage Capacity objects.
enrichment.fix: The API server now emits a deprecation warning whenever these objects reference the node beta label, alerting users to stop using it before it is removed.
enrichment.impact: Cluster operators receive early notice about the deprecated label usage, allowing them to update manifests and avoid future breakage or unexpected scheduling behavior.

other.description: API server's deprecated `--service-account-api-audiences` flag was removed.  Use `--api-audiences` instead.
other.author: ialidzhikov
other.userFacingChange: action required: API server's deprecated `--service-account-api-audiences` flag is now removed.  Use `--api-audiences` instead.

enrichment.problem: The kube-apiserver flag `--service-account-api-audiences` was deprecated and has now been removed, causing API server startup failures or ignored configuration for clusters that still specify this flag.
enrichment.affected: Administrators and operators who configured kube-apiserver with the `--service-account-api-audiences` flag.
enrichment.fix: Update the API server startup configuration to replace `--service-account-api-audiences` with the new `--api-audiences` flag, which serves the same purpose for service account token audience validation.
enrichment.impact: Clusters that relied on the removed flag must adjust their manifests or scripts. After the change, the API server starts correctly and token audience validation continues to work using the unified `--api-audiences` flag.

other.description: Deprecated beta APIs scheduled for removal in 1.25 are no longer served. See https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/deprecation-guide/#v1-25 for more information.
other.author: deads2k

enrichment.problem: Beta APIs that were scheduled for removal in Kubernetes 1.25 are still reachable in earlier releases, so clusters that have not been updated may be using APIs that are slated for deletion, leading to unexpected failures when the APIs disappear.
enrichment.affected: Clients, controllers, or custom scripts that use the beta APIs slated for removal in v1.25 will receive errors when trying to access those resources.
enrichment.fix: The APIs marked for removal in v1.25 are no longer served by the kube-apiserver. Any request to those beta endpoints now returns a NotFound error, completing the deprecation lifecycle.
enrichment.impact: Clusters or automation that still depend on the removed beta endpoints will start failing and must be migrated to the corresponding stable (v1) APIs. This enforces the deprecation policy and avoids a sudden breakage later.

other.description: Shell completion is now provided for the "--subresource" flag.
other.author: marckhouzam

enrichment.problem: kubectl's '--subresource' flag lacked shell auto‑completion, requiring users to manually type or remember possible subresource values.
enrichment.affected: kubectl users who invoke commands with the '--subresource' flag (e.g., get, edit, patch subresources).
enrichment.fix: Added shell completion support for the '--subresource' flag, enabling Bash/Zsh/Fish completions to suggest valid subresource names.
enrichment.impact: Improves command‑line usability for kubectl users, reducing typing effort and errors when working with subresources such as status, scale, or custom subresource endpoints.

other.description: Default burst limit for the discovery client set to 300.
other.author: ulucinar
other.userFacingChange: Default burst limit for the discovery client is now 300.

enrichment.problem: The discovery client had a low default burst limit, which could cause request throttling and slower API discovery for tools that make many discovery calls.
enrichment.affected: Users of the client-go discovery client, including kubectl and other tools that perform API discovery.
enrichment.fix: The default burst limit for the discovery client has been increased to 300, allowing more concurrent discovery requests without throttling.
enrichment.impact: Improves performance of kubectl and any client-go based tools that rely on discovery, especially in large clusters or automation scripts that issue many discovery requests.

other.description: For resources built into an apiserver, the server now logs at `-v=3` whether it is using watch caching.
other.author: MikeSpreitzer

enrichment.problem: Operators could not tell from logs whether the apiserver was serving watch requests from the watch cache for built‑in resources, making debugging watch performance difficult.
enrichment.affected: Kubernetes administrators and developers who rely on watch semantics for controllers or custom tooling, especially when diagnosing performance or correctness of watch handling.
enrichment.fix: The apiserver now emits a log entry at verbosity level 3 indicating whether watch caching is being used for each built‑in resource.
enrichment.impact: Improves observability and debugging of watch‑related latency or load issues, allowing clusters to be tuned more effectively.

other.description: Removed deprecated kubectl.kubernetes.io/default-logs-container support
other.author: pacoxu
other.userFacingChange: remove deprecated kubectl.kubernetes.io/default-logs-container support

enrichment.problem: The kubectl.kubernetes.io/default-logs-container annotation, which allowed kubectl logs to pick a default container, was deprecated and is no longer supported, causing commands that relied on it to fail or select the wrong container.
enrichment.affected: Users who set the kubectl.kubernetes.io/default-logs-container annotation on pods (or in CI pipelines) and expect kubectl logs to automatically select that container.
enrichment.fix: The code that recognized and processed the deprecated annotation has been removed. Users must now specify the desired container explicitly (e.g., kubectl logs -c <container>) or use other supported mechanisms.
enrichment.impact: Users who previously relied on the annotation need to update their workflows or pod specs. The change simplifies kubectl code and eliminates maintenance of a deprecated feature.

other.description: kubelet's deprecated `--experimental-kernel-memcg-notification` flag is now removed.  Use `--kernel-memcg-notification` instead.
other.author: ialidzhikov

enrichment.problem: The kubelet flag `--experimental-kernel-memcg-notification` was removed, causing kubelet startup failures for clusters that still reference this deprecated flag.
enrichment.affected: Clusters with kubelet configurations that still specify `--experimental-kernel-memcg-notification`. The change impacts node agents during startup.
enrichment.fix: The flag has been eliminated; users must replace it with the supported `--kernel-memcg-notification` flag in their kubelet configuration.
enrichment.impact: Prevents kubelet launch errors and aligns node configuration with the stable flag, ensuring proper kernel memory cgroup notifications without breaking existing workloads that adopt the new flag.

other.description: Feature gates that graduated to GA in 1.23 or earlier and were unconditionally enabled have been removed: CSIServiceAccountToken, ConfigurableFSGroupPolicy, EndpointSlice, EndpointSliceNodeName, EndpointSliceProxying, GenericEphemeralVolume, IPv6DualStack, IngressClassNamespacedParams, StorageObjectInUseProtection, TTLAfterFinished, VolumeSubpath, WindowsEndpointSliceProxying.
other.author: pohly

enrichment.problem: Feature gates that had already graduated to GA in 1.23 or earlier were still present in the code base and could be set manually, creating unnecessary configuration noise and potential confusion for users.
enrichment.affected: Users who manually set or relied on the now‑removed feature‑gate flags in kube-apiserver (or other control‑plane components) during upgrades or custom deployments.
enrichment.fix: The now-unconditional, GA feature gates have been removed from the source code and from the list of configurable feature gates.
enrichment.impact: Cluster upgrades no longer need to consider these gates, reducing the surface area for misconfiguration and simplifying the kube-apiserver feature‑gate list. No runtime behavior changes for workloads.

other.description: Kubernetes binaries are now built-in `module` mode instead of `GOPATH` mode.
other.author: liggitt
other.userFacingChange: Kubernetes binaries are now built in module mode instead of GOPATH mode

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes binaries were built using the legacy GOPATH mode, which required a specific workspace layout and could lead to inconsistent builds and dependency issues for developers and CI systems.
enrichment.affected: Anyone building Kubernetes binaries – developers, CI systems, and distribution packagers – are affected by the new build process.
enrichment.fix: The build process has been switched to Go module mode, allowing the binaries to be compiled directly with go modules without needing a GOPATH workspace. This aligns the build with modern Go practices.
enrichment.impact: Builds are now more reproducible, faster, and easier to set up. Developers, CI pipelines, and downstream packagers no longer need to manage GOPATH, reducing build failures and simplifying contribution onboarding.

other.description: Renamed `apiserver_watch_cache_watch_cache_initializations_total` to `apiserver_watch_cache_initializations_total`
other.author: logicalhan
other.userFacingChange: Rename apiserver_watch_cache_watch_cache_initializations_total to apiserver_watch_cache_initializations_total

enrichment.problem: The metric name `apiserver_watch_cache_watch_cache_initializations_total` was misleading/duplicated, causing confusion for users querying or alerting on watch cache initialization metrics.
enrichment.affected: Any monitoring setup that scraped kube-apiserver metrics and referenced the old metric name; operators and developers using those metrics for alerting or dashboards.
enrichment.fix: The metric has been renamed to `apiserver_watch_cache_initializations_total`, simplifying the name while preserving the same semantics and data collection.
enrichment.impact: Prometheus users, alerting rules, and dashboards that referenced the old metric name must be updated to the new name to continue receiving correct data. No functional change to the apiserver behavior.

other.description: Kube-controller-manager: Removed flags  `deleting-pods-qps`, `deleting-pods-burst`, and `register-retry-count`.
other.author: pandaamanda
other.userFacingChange: kube-controller-manager:  'deleting-pods-qps'  'deleting-pods-burst'  'register-retry-count' flags are removed.

enrichment.problem: The kube-controller-manager flags `deleting-pods-qps`, `deleting-pods-burst`, and `register-retry-count` were removed, so any deployment that still specifies them will fail to start because the flags are unrecognized.
enrichment.affected: Clusters running kube-controller-manager with the now-removed flags in their static pod manifests, systemd units, or helm charts.
enrichment.fix: The flags have been eliminated from the binary; users must delete those flag definitions from their manifests or command-line invocations. No functional change to controller behaviour is required.
enrichment.impact: Clusters that relied on these flags must update their kube-controller-manager configuration. The removal simplifies the binary and eliminates dead code.

other.description: Deleted the `apimachinery/clock` package. Please use `k8s.io/utils/clock` package instead.
other.author: MadhavJivrajani
other.userFacingChange: apimachinery/clock: This deletes the apimachinery/clock package. Please use k8s.io/utils/clock instead.

issueContext.title: There are two clock packages with divergent history
issueContext.body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


**What happened**:
I discovered a need to update one of the two clock packages, and preparation for that revealed the divergent history of the two.

One line of development can be seen in
- https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/commits/0fdb33b25e3cb207705f225aec7d30b900dd1e89/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/util/clock/clock.go , and then
- https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/commits/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/clock/clock.go

It looks like early on that was cloned into k8s.io/utils, and from there we have an independent line of development:
- https://github.com/kubernetes/utils/commits/master/clock/testing/fake_clock.go

**What you expected to happen**:
The two clock packages would be kept in sync for a while and then one removed.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

**Anything else we need to know?**:

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`):
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration:
- OS (e.g: `cat /etc/os-release`):
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`):
- Install tools:
- Network plugin and version (if this is a network-related bug):
- Others:

enrichment.problem: The apimachinery/clock package duplicated functionality already provided by k8s.io/utils/clock, leading to divergent histories and potential confusion for developers.
enrichment.affected: Developers and components that referenced apimachinery/pkg/util/clock, such as parts of apimachinery, client-go, and any external code relying on that import.
enrichment.fix: The apimachinery/clock package has been removed. Code should be updated to import and use the k8s.io/utils/clock package instead.
enrichment.impact: Any code (including Kubernetes core components or external projects) that imported apimachinery/clock will fail to compile until the import is changed. The change simplifies the codebase and eliminates maintenance of two separate clock implementations.

other.description: Changed PV framework delete timeout to 5 minutes as documented.
other.author: saikat-royc
other.userFacingChange: honor the framework delete timeout for pv

enrichment.problem: The PersistentVolume (PV) framework delete timeout was not being honoured, causing PV deletions to potentially stall beyond the intended limit.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that delete PersistentVolumes (e.g., via PVC deletion or manual PV removal) could see delayed cleanup.
enrichment.fix: The PV controller now respects the configured framework delete timeout, set to the documented 5‑minute default.
enrichment.impact: PV deletions now complete within the expected time window, preventing lingering PV objects and improving storage resource cleanup.

other.description: Add missing powershell option to kubectl completion command short description.
other.author: danielhelfand

enrichment.problem: The short description for the `kubectl completion` command omitted the PowerShell option, so users were not informed about PowerShell support for shell completion.
enrichment.affected: Windows users of kubectl who rely on shell completion, especially those using PowerShell.
enrichment.fix: The missing PowerShell option is added to the short description of the `kubectl completion` command, making the documentation complete.
enrichment.impact: Improves the usability of kubectl on Windows PowerShell by clearly exposing the completion option, reducing confusion for CLI users.

other.description: The beta `PodSecurityPolicy` admission plugin, deprecated since 1.21, is removed. Follow the instructions at https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/migrate-from-psp/ to migrate to the built-in PodSecurity admission plugin (or to another third-party  policy webhook) prior to upgrading to v1.25.
other.author: liggitt
other.userFacingChange: The beta `PodSecurityPolicy` admission plugin, deprecated since 1.21, is removed. Follow the instructions at https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/migrate-from-psp/ to migrate to the built-in PodSecurity admission plugin (or to another third-party policy webhook) prior to upgrading to v1.25.

enrichment.problem: The beta PodSecurityPolicy (PSP) admission plugin, which was deprecated in v1.21, has been removed in v1.25. Clusters that still have PSP enabled will encounter admission failures for pods that rely on PSP rules.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that have the PSP admission plugin enabled and any workloads that depend on PSP rules for pod security.
enrichment.fix: Migrate to the built-in PodSecurity admission plugin or to an alternative third‑party policy webhook before upgrading to v1.25, following the migration guide at https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/migrate-from-psp/.
enrichment.impact: Ensures cluster security policies continue to be enforced after the upgrade. Prevents pod creation failures and unintentional loss of policy enforcement for clusters that have not migrated.

other.description: Updated cri-tools to [v1.24.2(https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/cri-tools/releases/tag/v1.24.2).
other.author: saschagrunert

enrichment.problem: Older cri-tools versions could contain bugs or lack support for newer CRI features, potentially causing issues with container runtime interactions.
enrichment.affected: Clusters running Kubernetes 1.24 that use the CRI (container runtime interface), especially those relying on kubelet for pod management.
enrichment.fix: The release updates cri-tools to version v1.24.2, bringing bug fixes, compatibility improvements, and new features from upstream.
enrichment.impact: Improves stability and compatibility of the container runtime interface used by kubelet and other node components, reducing the risk of runtime‑related failures.

other.description: The `gcp` and `azure` auth plugins have been removed from client-go and kubectl. See https://github.com/Azure/kubelogin and https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/containers-kubernetes/kubectl-auth-changes-in-gke
other.author: enj

issueContext.title: Remove gcp and azure auth plugins in v1.25
issueContext.body:
This serves as a milestoned issue to track removal of gcp and azure auth plugin code per #102181

/assign
/milestone v1.25

enrichment.problem: The built‑in GCP and Azure authentication plugins were removed from client-go and kubectl, so clusters that relied on the in‑tree plugins can no longer authenticate using the previous configuration.
enrichment.affected: Any user or automation that authenticates to a GKE cluster with the built‑in gcp auth plugin or to an AKS cluster with the built‑in azure auth plugin. Scripts, CI pipelines, and third‑party tools that assume the plugins are present are affected.
enrichment.fix: Authentication must now be performed via the external plugins: use the GCP gcloud credential helper or the Azure kubelogin binary (https://github.com/Azure/kubelogin) and configure the kubeconfig to point to these executables.
enrichment.impact: Users upgrading to v1.25 who depend on the in‑tree GCP or Azure auth plugins will see authentication failures until they switch to the external helpers. The change simplifies the code base and aligns Kubernetes with the cloud providers’ own authentication tooling.

other.description: kubeadm: perform additional dockershim cleanup. Treat all container runtimes as remote by using the flag "--container-runtime=remote", given dockershim was removed in 1.24 and given kubeadm 1.25 supports a kubelet version of 1.24 and 1.25. The flag "--network-plugin" will no longer be used for new clusters. Stop cleaning up the following dockershim related directories on "kubeadm reset": "/var/lib/dockershim", "/var/runkubernetes", "/var/lib/cni"
other.author: neolit123

enrichment.problem: kubeadm assumed Docker's dockershim was present, cleaning up dockershim directories and using the "--network-plugin" flag, which caused errors or unnecessary deletions after dockershim was removed in Kubernetes 1.24.
enrichment.affected: Users initializing or resetting clusters with kubeadm 1.25 that rely on non‑Docker container runtimes (containerd, cri‑o, etc.).
enrichment.fix: kubeadm now treats all container runtimes as remote with "--container-runtime=remote", stops using "--network-plugin" for new clusters, and no longer removes dockershim‑related directories ("/var/lib/dockershim", "/var/run/kubernetes", "/var/lib/cni") during "kubeadm reset".
enrichment.impact: Cluster initialization and reset work correctly with any CRI (e.g., containerd) on kubeadm 1.25, preventing failures and accidental data loss caused by stale dockershim cleanup.

other.description: kubeadm: stop applying the `node-role.kubernetes.io/master:NoSchedule` taint to control plane nodes for new clusters. Remove the taint from existing control plane nodes during "kubeadm upgrade apply"
other.author: neolit123
other.userFacingChange: kubeadm: stop applying the "node-role.kubernetes.io/master:NoSchedule" taint to control plane nodes for new clusters. Remove the taint from existing control plane nodes during "kubeadm upgrade apply"

enrichment.problem: kubeadm applied the 'node-role.kubernetes.io/master:NoSchedule' taint to control‑plane nodes, preventing regular pods from being scheduled onto them. This caused extra steps for users who wanted workloads on control‑plane nodes, especially in single‑node clusters or when upgrading existing clusters.
enrichment.affected: Users who create clusters with kubeadm or upgrade existing kubeadm‑managed clusters; control‑plane nodes that previously carried the master taint; any pods that need to run on those nodes.
enrichment.fix: kubeadm no longer adds the master NoSchedule taint when creating new clusters, and during 'kubeadm upgrade apply' it automatically removes the taint from existing control‑plane nodes.
enrichment.impact: Workloads can now run on control‑plane nodes without manual taint removal, simplifying single‑node and small‑cluster deployments and reducing operational friction after upgrades.

other.description:
Some apiserver metrics were changed, as follows.
- `priority_level_seat_count_samples` is replaced with `priority_level_seat_utilization`, which samples every nanosecond rather than every millisecond; the old metric conveyed utilization despite its name.
- `priority_level_seat_count_watermarks` is removed.
- `priority_level_request_count_samples` is replaced with `priority_level_request_utilization`, which samples every nanosecond rather than every millisecond; the old metric conveyed utilization despite its name.
- `priority_level_request_count_watermarks` is removed.
- `read_vs_write_request_count_samples` is replaced with `read_vs_write_current_requests`, which samples every nanosecond rather than every second; the new metric, like the old one, measures utilization when the max-in-flight filter is used and number of requests when the API Priority and Fairness filter is used.
- `read_vs_write_request_count_watermarks` is removed.
other.author: MikeSpreitzer
other.userFacingChange:
Some apiserver metrics were changed, as follows.
- `priority_level_seat_count_samples` is replaced with `priority_level_seat_utilization`, which samples every nanosecond rather than every millisecond; the old metric conveyed utilization despite its name.
- `priority_level_seat_count_watermarks` is removed.
- `priority_level_request_count_samples` is replaced with `priority_level_request_utilization`, which samples every nanosecond rather than every millisecond; the old metric conveyed utilization despite its name.
- `priority_level_request_count_watermarks` is removed.
- `read_vs_write_request_count_samples` is replaced with `read_vs_write_current_requests`, which samples every nanosecond rather than every second; the new metric, like the old one, measures utilization when the max-in-flight filter is used and number of requests when the API Priority and Fairness filter is used.
- `read_vs_write_request_count_watermarks` is removed.

enrichment.problem: Existing apiserver metrics had misleading names and coarse sampling intervals, and included watermarks that were no longer needed, causing confusion and less precise monitoring for API Priority and Fairness behavior.
enrichment.affected: Operators and developers who scrape kube-apiserver metrics for API Priority and Fairness monitoring, as well as any alerting rules or dashboards referencing the removed or renamed metrics.
enrichment.fix: Replaced `priority_level_seat_count_samples` with `priority_level_seat_utilization` and `priority_level_request_count_samples` with `priority_level_request_utilization`, both sampling at nanosecond granularity. Replaced `read_vs_write_request_count_samples` with `read_vs_write_current_requests` also sampling at nanoseconds. Removed the corresponding watermarks metrics. The new names reflect true utilization semantics and provide higher‑resolution data.
enrichment.impact: Monitoring, alerting, and dashboard configurations that rely on the old metric names or sampling rates need to be updated, but users gain more accurate and intuitively named metrics for capacity planning and troubleshooting API request handling.

other.description:
`apiserver_longrunning_gauge` was removed from the codebase. Please use `apiserver_longrunning_requests`
instead.
other.author: logicalhan
other.userFacingChange: apiserver_longrunning_gauge is removed from the codebase. Please use apiserver_longrunning_requests instead.

enrichment.problem: The metric `apiserver_longrunning_gauge` was removed from the codebase, breaking any monitoring setups that still reference it.
enrichment.affected: Any cluster monitoring solution or custom script that queries `apiserver_longrunning_gauge` from the API server. This includes Prometheus, Grafana dashboards, and alerting rules.
enrichment.fix: The metric has been eliminated; users should switch to the new `apiserver_longrunning_requests` metric, which provides equivalent information.
enrichment.impact: Monitoring and alerting systems that scrape the old metric will stop receiving data, requiring updates to dashboards, alerts, and scrape configurations to continue observing long‑running request behavior.

other.description: Kubeadm: graduated the kubeadm specific feature gate `UnversionedKubeletConfigMap` to GA and locked it to `true` by default. The kubelet related ConfigMap and RBAC rules are now locked to have a simplified naming `*kubelet-config` instead of the legacy naming `*kubelet-config-x.yy`, where `x.yy` was the version of the control plane. If you have previously used the old naming format with `UnversionedKubeletConfigMap=false`, you must manually copy the config map from `kube-system/kubelet-config-x.yy` to `kube-system/kubelet-config` before upgrading to `v1.25`.
other.author: neolit123
other.userFacingChange: kubeadm: graduate the kubeadm specific feature gate UnversionedKubeletConfigMap to GA and lock it to "true" by default. The kubelet related ConfigMap and RBAC rules are now locked to have a simplified naming "*kubelet-config" instead of the legacy naming "*kubelet-config-x.yy", where "x.yy" was the version of the control plane. If you have previously used the old naming format with UnversionedKubeletConfigMap=false, you must manually copy the config map from kube-system/kubelet-config-x.yy to kube-system/kubelet-config before upgrading to 1.25.

enrichment.problem: Clusters upgraded to v1.25 that had the UnversionedKubeletConfigMap feature gate disabled and were using the legacy versioned ConfigMap name (kube-system/kubelet-config-x.yy) will lose their kubelet configuration because kubeadm now expects an unversioned ConfigMap named kube-system/kubelet-config.
enrichment.affected: Clusters upgrading to v1.25 that previously disabled UnversionedKubeletConfigMap and used version‑specific kubelet ConfigMap names. The nodes’ kubelet processes are directly impacted.
enrichment.fix: The feature gate UnversionedKubeletConfigMap has been graduated to GA and locked to true. The kubelet ConfigMap and associated RBAC objects are now always created with the simplified name *kubelet-config. Users must manually copy their existing versioned ConfigMap to the new unversioned name before upgrading to v1.25 if they had the gate set to false.
enrichment.impact: Ensures a consistent, version‑agnostic naming scheme for kubelet configuration, simplifying future upgrades. Without the manual copy step, nodes may start without the intended kubelet configuration, potentially leading to misconfiguration or kubelet start failures after upgrade.

other.description:
In "large" clusters, kube-proxy in iptables mode will now sometimes
leave unused rules in iptables for a while (up to `--iptables-sync-period`)
before deleting them. This improves performance by not requiring it to
check for stale rules on every sync. (In smaller clusters, it will still
remove unused rules immediately once they are no longer used.)

(The threshold for "large" used here is currently "1000 endpoints" but
this is subject to change.)
other.author: danwinship
other.userFacingChange:
In "large" clusters, kube-proxy in iptables mode will now sometimes
leave unused rules in iptables for a while (up to `--iptables-sync-period`)
before deleting them. This improves performance by not requiring it to
check for stale rules on every sync. (In smaller clusters, it will still
remove unused rules immediately once they are no longer used.)

(The threshold for "large" used here is currently "1000 endpoints" but
this is subject to change.)

enrichment.problem: In large clusters, kube-proxy in iptables mode checked for stale iptables rules on every sync, causing unnecessary CPU and latency overhead.
enrichment.affected: Clusters with >1000 service endpoints that run kube-proxy in iptables mode. All pods and services that rely on iptables‑based traffic proxying are indirectly affected.
enrichment.fix: kube-proxy now defers removal of unused iptables rules for up to the `--iptables-sync-period` when the cluster has more than 1000 endpoints, eliminating the per‑sync stale‑rule scan. Small clusters continue to delete rules immediately.
enrichment.impact: Reduces kube-proxy CPU usage and sync latency in large clusters, improving overall network performance while still eventually cleaning up stale rules. No functional change for traffic; only a performance improvement.

other.description: `apiserver_dropped_requests` is dropped from this release since `apiserver_request_total` can now be used to track dropped requests. `etcd_object_counts` is also removed in favor of `apiserver_storage_objects`. `apiserver_registered_watchers` is also removed in favor of `apiserver_longrunning_requests`.

enrichment.problem: The release removes three apiserver metrics (apiserver_dropped_requests, etcd_object_counts, apiserver_registered_watchers). Existing monitoring, dashboards, or alerts that depend on these metrics will stop receiving data.
enrichment.affected: Clusters with monitoring or alerting setups that scrape these specific apiserver metrics. Any tooling, dashboards, or alerts that query the dropped metrics will be affected.
enrichment.fix: The deprecated metrics are dropped. Users should switch to the recommended replacements: use apiserver_request_total to count dropped requests, apiserver_storage_objects instead of etcd_object_counts, and apiserver_longrunning_requests instead of apiserver_registered_watchers.
enrichment.impact: Monitoring and alerting configurations that reference the removed metrics will need to be updated to the new metrics to avoid gaps in visibility. No functional impact on cluster operation.

enrichment.affected: All clusters running a kubelet; operators and tools that parse kubelet logs are affected by the reduced verbosity.

other.description: kube-proxy: The "userspace" proxy-mode is deprecated on Linux and Windows, despite being the default on Windows.  As of v1.26, the default mode for Windows will change to 'kernelspace'.
other.author: pandaamanda

enrichment.problem: The userspace kube-proxy mode is deprecated on both Linux and Windows, but Windows clusters still default to userspace. Starting with v1.26 the default for Windows will switch to kernelspace, which can cause unexpected behavior for clusters that rely on the userspace default.
enrichment.affected: Clusters running Windows nodes that rely on the default userspace kube-proxy mode.
enrichment.fix: Deprecate the userspace proxy mode and change the default proxy mode for Windows from userspace to kernelspace in v1.26. Administrators can continue using userspace mode by explicitly setting the mode.
enrichment.impact: Windows workloads will benefit from the more performant kernelspace proxy and align with Linux behavior. Clusters that depend on the userspace default need to update their configuration to avoid service disruption.

other.description: Improved `kubectl run` and `kubectl debug` error messages upon attaching failures.
other.author: soltysh
other.userFacingChange: Improve kubectl run and debug attach problems error

enrichment.problem: When `kubectl run` or `kubectl debug` failed to attach to a container, the error messages were vague, making it difficult for users to understand why the attach operation failed.
enrichment.affected: Users who run `kubectl run` or `kubectl debug` and encounter attach failures, typically when debugging pods or launching one‑off containers.
enrichment.fix: The commands now emit clearer, more specific error messages for attach failures, helping users identify the root cause more quickly.
enrichment.impact: Improves the debugging experience for developers and operators, reducing time spent troubleshooting attach failures with `kubectl run` and `kubectl debug`.

other.description: The kubelet no longer supports collecting accelerator metrics through cAdvisor. The feature gate `DisableAcceleratorUsageMetrics` is now GA and cannot be disabled.
other.author: pacoxu

enrichment.problem: Kubelet stopped collecting accelerator (e.g., GPU) usage metrics via cAdvisor. Monitoring tools that relied on these metrics can no longer retrieve them.
enrichment.affected: Clusters running workloads that depend on accelerator usage metrics exposed by cAdvisor, such as GPU‑heavy applications with Prometheus scrapes of kubelet metrics.
enrichment.fix: The `DisableAcceleratorUsageMetrics` feature gate is now GA and permanently enabled, removing the cAdvisor accelerator metric collection path.
enrichment.impact: Users lose built‑in visibility of accelerator resource usage from kubelet metrics and must adopt alternative sources (e.g., device plugin metrics, external exporters) for monitoring and autoscaling.

other.description: Windows winkernel kube-proxy no longer supports Windows HNS v1 APIs.
other.author: papagalu

enrichment.problem: kube-proxy running on Windows with the winkernel datapath relied on the legacy Windows Host Network Service (HNS) v1 APIs, which are no longer supported.
enrichment.affected: Windows nodes running kube-proxy with the winkernel datapath that depend on HNS v1 APIs.
enrichment.fix: The change removes support for HNS v1 APIs from the Windows winkernel kube-proxy implementation. Users must migrate to the newer HNS v2 APIs for kube-proxy to function on Windows nodes.
enrichment.impact: Windows clusters that still use HNS v1 will see kube-proxy stop working, breaking Service traffic routing. Migrating to HNS v2 restores functionality.

other.description: In the event that more than one IngressClass is designated "default", the DefaultIngressClass admission controller will choose one rather than fail.
other.author: kidddddddddddddddddddddd

enrichment.problem: When a cluster had more than one IngressClass object marked as the default, the DefaultIngressClass admission controller would reject the creation of Ingress resources instead of handling the ambiguity.
enrichment.affected: Clusters with multiple IngressClass resources marked as default; users creating Ingress objects in such clusters.
enrichment.fix: The DefaultIngressClass admission controller now deterministically selects one of the default IngressClass objects and allows the Ingress to be admitted, rather than failing the request.
enrichment.impact: Ingress resources can be created even if multiple IngressClass objects are marked default, preventing unexpected admission failures and improving cluster reliability for users deploying multiple ingress controllers.

other.description: For Linux, `kube-proxy` uses a new “distroless” container image, instead of an image based on Debian.

enrichment.affected: All clusters running kube-proxy on Linux nodes. The change is transparent to workloads but may affect custom images that relied on Debian tooling inside the proxy container.
enrichment.fix: Replaced the Debian‑based image with a minimal “distroless” image for the Linux kube-proxy binary.
enrichment.impact: Reduces the size of the kube-proxy image, shortens pull times, and lowers the security footprint by removing unnecessary packages. No functional behavior change for existing deployments.

issueContext.title: kubectl create help implies a list of service accounts can be references in a clusterrolebinding
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

I'm not sure whether this is the documentation being unclear, or a bug with kubectl itself but I suspect the former.

Given this help page
```bash
$ kubectl create clusterrolebinding --help
Create a cluster role binding for a particular cluster role.
# Omitted for brevity
      --serviceaccount=[]: Service accounts to bind to the clusterrole, in the format <namespace>:<name>
```
I expected to be able to use
```bash
$ kubectl create clusterrolebinding pipelineSAs --clusterrole=view --serviceaccount=["ns1:pipeline", "ns2:pipeline"]
```
Instead I got the following error
```bash
$ kubectl create clusterrolebinding pipelinesas --clusterrole=view --serviceaccount=["ns1:pipeline", "ns2:pipeline"]
error: exactly one NAME is required, got 2
See 'kubectl create clusterrolebinding -h' for help and examples
```

### What did you expect to happen?

To get the same output as defining the flag twice

aka
```bash
$ kubectl create clusterrolebinding pipelinesas --clusterrole=view --serviceaccount=ns1:pipeline --serviceaccount=ns2:pipeline
clusterrolebinding.rbac.authorization.k8s.io/pipelinesas created
```
and

```bash
$ kubectl create clusterrolebinding pipelineSAs --clusterrole=view --serviceaccount=["ns1:pipeline", "ns2:pipeline"]
clusterrolebinding.rbac.authorization.k8s.io/pipelinesas created
```
should give the same output, or the help page shouldn't list `[]` as the parameter type for --serviceaccount

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

```bash
kubectl create ns ns1 
kubectl create ns ns2
kubectl --namespace ns1 create sa pipeline
kubectl --namespace ns2 create sa pipeline
kubectl create clusterrolebinding pipelineSAs --clusterrole=view --serviceaccount=["ns1:pipeline", "ns2:pipeline"]
```

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_
