issueContext.title: misleading comments in container.Ports
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

The comments in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/dc96c3dfccbc2005e4c4367fc8da199413e2bdcb/staging/src/k8s.io/api/core/v1/types.go#L2328 says that : 
```
Exposing a port here gives
the system additional information about the network connections a
container uses, but is primarily informational.
```
However there are several cases where this is false : 
- When using a Service with a targetPort that references a name in the ports arrays of the pod.
- Some software (ab)uses this API to get which ports are used (See https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/108131 Although unfixable, my goal is to fix the documentation so other people don't have the same problem). The Azure Load Balancer implementation does this for instance.
- Some other network/security software might use this information.

Also, is it possible to document/reference the above issue in the comment ? 

### What did you expect to happen?

Since it is described as *informational* I expected for the network to work without this information. But it's definitely not the case.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

securityFixes.title: Aggregated API server can cause clients to be redirected (SSRF)
securityFixes.description:
A security issue was discovered in kube-apiserver that could allow an attacker controlled aggregated API server to redirect client traffic to any URL.  This could lead to the client performing unexpected actions as well as leaking the client's credentials to third parties. 

There is no mitigation from this issue.  Cluster admins should take care to secure aggregated API servers and should not grant access to mutate `APIService`s to untrusted parties.

apiChange.description: Revert regression that prevented client-go latency metrics to be reported with a template URL to avoid label cardinality.
apiChange.author: aanm

enrichment.problem: A regression stopped client-go from emitting latency metrics, so the metrics were not reported and the intended templated URL (used to keep label cardinality low) was not applied.
enrichment.affected: Any workloads or controllers that use client-go for API calls and rely on its latency metrics for observability.
enrichment.fix: The regression is reverted, restoring the original code path so client-go once again records latency metrics with the template URL, preserving low label cardinality.
enrichment.impact: Restores visibility into client-go request latency for operators and developers, enabling accurate monitoring and alerting of API communication performance.

enrichment.fix: The build process has been updated to use Go 1.19.1 for compiling all Kubernetes components.

bugOrRegression.description: Adds back in unused flags on kubectl run command, which did not go through the required deprecation period before being removed.
bugOrRegression.author: brianpursley

enrichment.problem: The kubectl run command had several flags removed without going through the required deprecation period, causing errors for users who still referenced those flags.
enrichment.affected: Users and automation that invoke `kubectl run` with the now‑restored flags.
enrichment.fix: Re‑introduce the previously removed, unused flags to the kubectl run command, restoring the original flag set and behavior.
enrichment.impact: Restores compatibility for scripts and workflows that relied on the missing flags and ensures the CLI follows proper deprecation policies, preventing unexpected command failures.

bugOrRegression.description: Avoid propagating hosts' `search .` into containers' `/etc/resolv.conf`
bugOrRegression.author: lucab

enrichment.problem: The host's resolv.conf entry `search .` was being copied into each container's /etc/resolv.conf, causing incorrect DNS search domain behavior inside pods.
enrichment.affected: All pods that rely on DNS resolution could experience lookup issues due to the propagated `search .` entry. The change affects workloads running on nodes where the host resolv.conf contains this entry.
enrichment.fix: Kubelet now filters out the `search .` entry when generating the pod's resolv.conf, ensuring containers only inherit appropriate DNS settings.
enrichment.impact: Pods receive correct DNS configuration, preventing resolution failures caused by an unwanted empty search domain. Improves reliability of service discovery for all workloads.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix an ephemeral port exhaustion bug caused by improper connection management that occurred when a large number of objects were handled by kubectl while exec auth was in use.
bugOrRegression.author: enj

enrichment.problem: kubectl leaked connections when handling a large number of objects while exec authentication was in use, leading to exhaustion of ephemeral ports and causing subsequent exec operations to fail.
enrichment.affected: Users invoking kubectl exec (especially in scripts or bulk operations) experienced failures due to exhausted ports. The issue impacted the kubectl client and the API server's exec authentication path.
enrichment.fix: Implemented proper connection management to ensure connections are closed/reused, preventing port leaks during bulk object handling with exec auth.
enrichment.impact: Restores reliable exec functionality for users running kubectl against many resources, eliminating failures caused by port exhaustion and improving overall CLI stability.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix problem in updating VolumeAttached in node status
bugOrRegression.author: xing-yang

enrichment.problem: Node status VolumeAttached information was not being updated correctly, causing the node to report stale or missing volume attachment data.
enrichment.affected: Workloads using persistent volumes (especially CSI volumes) on nodes where the attach‑detach controller updates node status.
enrichment.fix: Corrected the logic that updates the `VolumesAttached` field in the node status, ensuring the attach‑detach controller records the current set of attached volumes accurately.
enrichment.impact: Pods that depend on CSI/PersistentVolumes can now be scheduled and started reliably because the scheduler and kubelet see the correct attachment state, preventing mount failures and unnecessary re‑attaches.

bugOrRegression.description: Kube-apiserver: redirect responses are no longer returned from backends by default. Set `--aggregator-reject-forwarding-redirect=false` to continue forwarding redirect responses.
bugOrRegression.author: enj

enrichment.problem: Starting with this release, the kube-apiserver no longer forwards HTTP redirect responses received from aggregated API backends. Clusters that relied on receiving redirect responses from these backends will see them rejected by default.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using the API aggregation layer where backend services return HTTP 3xx redirects. Clients expecting those redirects will be affected.
enrichment.fix: The default behavior was changed to reject redirects. A new flag `--aggregator-reject-forwarding-redirect` can be set to `false` to restore the previous forwarding behavior for those who need it.
enrichment.impact: Improves security by preventing unintended open‑redirects from aggregated APIs, but may require a configuration change for existing setups that depend on redirect handling, avoiding potential service disruptions.

bugOrRegression.description: Allow Label section in vsphere e2e cloudprovider configuration
bugOrRegression.author: gnufied

enrichment.problem: The vSphere e2e cloud‑provider test configuration did not support a label section, preventing tests from specifying node labels via the cloud‑provider config.
enrichment.affected: Developers and CI pipelines that run vSphere e2e cloud‑provider tests; any workloads that rely on label handling in vSphere clusters.
enrichment.fix: Add a `label` section to the vSphere e2e cloud‑provider configuration schema and implement its handling, allowing users to define labels in the cloud‑provider config for e2e tests.
enrichment.impact: Enables testing and validation of label‑related functionality (e.g., topology, node‑selection) in vSphere environments, improving test coverage and developer confidence.

bugOrRegression.description: Correct the calculating error in podTopologySpread plugin to avoid unexpected scheduling results.
bugOrRegression.author: kerthcet

enrichment.problem: The podTopologySpread plugin had a calculation error that could cause pods to be scheduled in a way that violated topology spread constraints, leading to uneven pod distribution.
enrichment.affected: Any workload that uses pod topology spread constraints (e.g., Deployments, StatefulSets, Jobs) could experience incorrect scheduling.
enrichment.fix: Fixed the calculation logic in the podTopologySpread plugin so that it correctly evaluates topology domains and respects spread constraints during scheduling.
enrichment.impact: Ensures pods are placed according to the intended topology spread constraints, preventing over‑concentration of pods on specific nodes or zones and improving reliability of workload distribution.

bugOrRegression.description: Kube-apiserver: gzip compression switched from level 4 to level 1 to improve large list call latencies in exchange for higher network bandwidth usage (10-50% higher). This increases the headroom before very large unpaged list calls exceed request timeout limits.
bugOrRegression.author: shyamjvs

enrichment.problem: Large unpaged list API calls experienced high latency and could exceed request timeout limits due to the default gzip compression level (level 4) used by kube-apiserver.
enrichment.affected: Any workload or tool that performs large unpaged list calls against the API server, especially in clusters with many objects.
enrichment.fix: The default gzip compression level is reduced from level 4 to level 1, decreasing CPU work and latency for large list responses. This trade‑off increases network bandwidth consumption by roughly 10‑50%.
enrichment.impact: Clients that list many resources (e.g., kubectl get pods -A, controllers) see lower latency and fewer timeout failures, improving reliability for large clusters. Administrators should anticipate a modest rise in outbound bandwidth from the apiserver.

bugOrRegression.description: Kube-apiserver: resolved a regression that treated `304 Not Modified` responses from aggregated API servers as internal errors
bugOrRegression.author: liggitt

enrichment.problem: kube-apiserver incorrectly treated HTTP 304 Not Modified responses from aggregated API servers as internal errors, causing clients to receive spurious error messages.
enrichment.affected: Any workloads, controllers, or users interacting with aggregated API servers that could receive 304 responses were impacted by false error reports.
enrichment.fix: The regression was fixed so that 304 responses from aggregated API servers are recognized as valid and no longer reported as internal server errors.
enrichment.impact: Clients and controllers that rely on aggregated APIs now receive correct responses, reducing false error handling and improving overall cluster reliability.

bugOrRegression.description: Kubeadm: allow RSA and ECDSA format keys in preflight check
bugOrRegression.author: SataQiu

enrichment.problem: kubeadm preflight checks rejected RSA and ECDSA formatted private keys, causing init/join failures for users who generated certificates with those key types.
enrichment.affected: Kubeadm users who create or use RSA/ECDSA private keys for cluster certificates during init or join operations.
enrichment.fix: The preflight validation logic was updated to accept RSA and ECDSA key formats, allowing kubeadm to proceed when such keys are present.
enrichment.impact: Users can now bootstrap or join clusters with RSA/ECDSA certificates without manual workarounds, improving usability and reducing setup errors.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix list cost estimation in Priority and Fairness for list requests with metadata.name specified.

enrichment.problem: The Priority and Fairness module incorrectly estimated the cost of list requests that included a metadata.name filter, leading to inaccurate request accounting and potentially improper throttling.

enrichment.fix: Adjusted the cost estimation logic in the API server's Priority and Fairness code to correctly handle list requests with metadata.name specified.
enrichment.impact: Ensures fair and accurate request throttling for clients using list operations with a name filter, preventing unnecessary request rejections or throttling and improving overall API reliability.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixes an issue in winkernel proxier that causes proxy rules to leak anytime service backends are modified.
bugOrRegression.author: daschott

enrichment.problem: The winkernel proxier in kube-proxy leaked proxy rules every time the set of service backends changed, causing stale rules and potential traffic routing issues on Windows nodes.
enrichment.affected: Kubernetes clusters that run Windows nodes using the winkernel mode of kube-proxy, especially when services are scaled or endpoints change.
enrichment.fix: The proxier logic was revised to correctly clean up and remove old proxy rules whenever service backends are modified.
enrichment.impact: Stops rule leakage, preserving correct service traffic routing and preventing memory/CPU resource waste on Windows clusters, improving stability and performance.

bugOrRegression.description: For raw block CSI volumes on Kubernetes, kubelet was incorrectly calling CSI NodeStageVolume for every single "map" (i.e. raw block "mount") operation for a volume already attached to the node. This PR ensures it is only called once per volume per node.
bugOrRegression.author: akankshakumari393

enrichment.problem: kubelet erroneously invoked CSI NodeStageVolume for every raw block volume "map" operation, even when the volume was already attached to the node, leading to redundant staging calls.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using raw block CSI volumes (block mode) that map the same volume multiple times on a node were affected by redundant NodeStageVolume calls.
enrichment.fix: The kubelet logic was updated to track staging per volume per node and invoke NodeStageVolume only once, preventing repeated calls for the same raw block volume.
enrichment.impact: Eliminates unnecessary CSI driver calls, reduces latency and load on the storage plugin, and avoids potential failures from repeated staging, improving reliability for workloads that use raw block CSI volumes.

bugOrRegression.description: Kube-scheduler: add taints filtering logic consistent with TaintToleration plugin for PodTopologySpread plugin
bugOrRegression.author: SataQiu

enrichment.problem: The PodTopologySpread plugin did not apply taint filtering consistently with the TaintToleration plugin, leading to pods being considered for topology spread across nodes they should not be scheduled on due to taints.
enrichment.affected: Kubernetes clusters where the PodTopologySpread plugin is used on pods that have tolerations or nodes with taints. The incorrect spread calculations could cause pods to land on unsuitable nodes.
enrichment.fix: Added taint filtering logic to the PodTopologySpread plugin that mirrors the behavior of the TaintToleration plugin, ensuring taints are respected during spread calculations.
enrichment.impact: Ensures pods are placed only on nodes that satisfy both topology spread constraints and taint tolerations, preventing unintended scheduling and improving cluster reliability.

bugOrRegression.description: This reverts https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/109706 and https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/111691 which caused https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/112793. I.e: the service controller to incorrectly sync load balancers for ExternalTrafficPolicy=Local under certain conditions
bugOrRegression.author: alexanderConstantinescu

enrichment.problem: The service controller incorrectly synchronized cloud load balancers for Services with ExternalTrafficPolicy=Local under certain conditions, leading to improper routing or loss of traffic.
enrichment.affected: Users running Service objects of type LoadBalancer with ExternalTrafficPolicy=Local on cloud providers (e.g., AWS, GCP) experienced incorrect load balancer configuration.
enrichment.fix: Reverted the two upstream changes (PR #109706 and PR #111691) that introduced the bug, restoring the original logic that correctly handles load balancer sync for ExternalTrafficPolicy=Local.
enrichment.impact: Restores correct load balancer behavior for LoadBalancer services using ExternalTrafficPolicy=Local, preventing traffic disruption and ensuring expected traffic distribution for affected workloads.

securityFixes.title: Unauthorized read of Custom Resources
securityFixes.description: A security issue was discovered in Kubernetes where users authorized to list or watch one type of namespaced custom resource cluster-wide can read custom resources of a different type in the same API group they are not authorized to read.

securityFixes.title: Node address isn't always verified when proxying
securityFixes.description:
A security issue was discovered in Kubernetes where users may have access to secure endpoints in the control plane network. Kubernetes clusters are only affected if an untrusted user can to modify Node objects and send requests proxying through them.

Kubernetes supports node proxying, which allows clients of kube-apiserver to access endpoints of a Kubelet to establish connections to Pods, retrieve container logs, and more. While Kubernetes already validates the proxying address for Nodes, a bug in kube-apiserver made it possible to bypass this validation. Bypassing this validation could allow authenticated requests destined for Nodes to be redirected to the API Server through its private network.

The merged fix enforces validation against the proxying address for a Node. In some cases, the fix can break clients that depend on the `nodes/proxy` subresource, specifically if a kubelet advertises a localhost or link-local address to the Kubernetes control plane. Configuring an egress proxy for egress to the cluster network can also mitigate this vulnerability.

apiChange.description: Protobuf serialization of metav1.MicroTime timestamps (used in `Lease` and `Event` API objects) has been corrected to truncate to microsecond precision, to match the documented behavior and JSON/YAML serialization. Any existing persisted data is truncated to microsecond when read from etcd.
apiChange.author: haoruan

enrichment.problem: Protobuf serialization of metav1.MicroTime timestamps used in Lease and Event objects did not truncate to microsecond precision, causing a mismatch with the documented behavior and JSON/YAML serialization.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that store or read Lease and Event objects (e.g., leader election, event recording) could see inconsistent timestamps before the fix.
enrichment.fix: The protobuf serializer now truncates MicroTime values to microsecond precision, matching JSON/YAML output. When reading existing data from etcd, timestamps are also truncated to microsecond precision.
enrichment.impact: Ensures consistent timestamp handling across protobuf, JSON, and YAML representations, preventing subtle bugs in components that rely on exact timestamp values such as leader election and event processing.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with Go 1.19.3
feature.author: xmudrii

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes binaries were being built with an older Go version, which could miss security patches, performance improvements, and future compatibility fixes provided by newer Go releases.
enrichment.affected: All clusters running Kubernetes binaries built with previous Go versions; every component compiled from source is affected.
enrichment.fix: The build process has been updated to use Go 1.19.3 for compiling all Kubernetes components.
enrichment.impact: All Kubernetes binaries (kube-apiserver, kube-controller-manager, kube-scheduler, kubelet, kube-proxy, kubectl, etc.) now incorporate security and performance updates from Go 1.19.3, reducing potential vulnerabilities and ensuring smoother operation on newer platforms.

bugOrRegression.description: Consider only plugin directory and not entire kubelet root when cleaning up mounts
bugOrRegression.author: mattcary

enrichment.problem: Kubelet's mount cleanup logic examined the entire kubelet root directory, which could unintentionally target and remove mounts that were not part of the volume plugin directory.
enrichment.affected: Nodes running the kubelet, especially those with custom or host-mounted volumes that could be mistakenly cleaned up.
enrichment.fix: The cleanup routine was updated to restrict its scope to only the plugin directory, leaving the rest of the kubelet root untouched during mount cleanup.
enrichment.impact: Prevents accidental deletion of unrelated mounts, reducing the risk of pod failures or node instability for workloads that rely on host or custom mounts.

bugOrRegression.description: Etcd: Update to v3.5.5
bugOrRegression.author: dims

enrichment.problem: Clusters running older etcd versions (e.g., v3.5.4) may be vulnerable to known bugs and security issues that could affect data integrity or availability.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes clusters that use the default etcd version bundled with the release (typically v3.5.4 or earlier).
enrichment.fix: Upgrade the bundled etcd binary to version v3.5.5, which includes upstream bug fixes and security patches.
enrichment.impact: Provides improved stability and protection against potential data loss or unauthorized access, ensuring more reliable operation of the Kubernetes control plane.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed a bug where a change in the `appProtocol` for a Service did not trigger a load balancer update.
bugOrRegression.author: MartinForReal

enrichment.problem: When the `appProtocol` field of a Service was changed, the cloud load balancer was not updated, leaving the load balancer configured with the old protocol and potentially breaking traffic routing.
enrichment.affected: Users with LoadBalancer Services that rely on the `appProtocol` field (e.g., HTTP/HTTPS) to control traffic handling were affected because protocol changes were silently ignored.
enrichment.fix: The Service controller now watches for changes to `appProtocol` and triggers a load balancer reconciliation, causing the external LB to be updated to match the new protocol.
enrichment.impact: Clusters that use Services of type LoadBalancer with custom `appProtocol` values will now see correct traffic handling after a protocol change, eliminating the need to recreate the Service to apply the update.

bugOrRegression.description: Kube-apiserver: DELETECOLLECTION API requests are now recorded in metrics with the correct verb.
bugOrRegression.author: sxllwx

enrichment.problem: DELETECOLLECTION API requests were logged in the apiserver request metrics with an incorrect verb, causing inaccurate monitoring data for collection‑wide delete operations.
enrichment.affected: Cluster administrators and any tooling that consumes apiserver request metrics (such as Prometheus dashboards and alerts) were seeing misleading data for DELETECOLLECTION calls.
enrichment.fix: The apiserver now records DELETECOLLECTION calls using the correct verb in the request metrics, aligning metric labels with the actual API operation performed.
enrichment.impact: Monitoring and alerting systems that rely on apiserver request metrics (e.g., Prometheus) will see accurate counts for collection delete operations, improving observability and troubleshooting without affecting API functionality.

bugOrRegression.description: Kube-apiserver: bugfix DeleteCollection API fails if request body is non-empty
bugOrRegression.author: sxllwx

enrichment.problem: The DeleteCollection REST endpoint in kube-apiserver returned an error when the request contained a non-empty body, causing API calls that include a body (e.g., dry‑run or client‑generated payloads) to fail.
enrichment.affected: Any workloads or controllers that invoke the DeleteCollection API with a request body were affected; the issue prevented successful deletions in those scenarios.
enrichment.fix: kube-apiserver was updated to ignore or correctly process a non‑empty request body for DeleteCollection, allowing the operation to succeed regardless of body content.
enrichment.impact: Clients and controllers that rely on DeleteCollection (such as batch deletions or garbage‑collection logic) can now use the API without encountering unexpected failures, improving reliability and compatibility.

bugOrRegression.description: Kube-proxy, will restart in case it detects that the Node assigned pod.Spec.PodCIDRs have changed
bugOrRegression.author: code-elinka

enrichment.problem: kube-proxy did not restart when a node's pod.Spec.PodCIDRs changed, leaving stale network rules and causing potential connectivity issues for pods on that node.
enrichment.affected: All nodes where the pod CIDR assignment changes, affecting pods that rely on kube-proxy for service traffic.
enrichment.fix: kube-proxy now watches the node's PodCIDR configuration and triggers a restart when a change is detected, ensuring it reloads its iptables/ipvs rules to reflect the new CIDRs.
enrichment.impact: Ensures correct traffic routing after pod CIDR updates, preventing service interruptions and network mis‑routing for workloads on affected nodes.

bugOrRegression.description: Kubelet: fix GetAllocatableCPUs method in cpumanager
bugOrRegression.author: Garrybest

enrichment.problem: The kubelet's GetAllocatableCPUs method in the CPU manager returned incorrect CPU capacity values, leading to inaccurate allocatable CPU reporting.
enrichment.affected: Nodes that run the kubelet with the CPU manager enabled, and any pods that request CPU resources on those nodes.
enrichment.fix: The GetAllocatableCPUs implementation has been corrected to compute and return the true set of allocatable CPUs based on the node's cgroup and CPU manager state.
enrichment.impact: Accurate CPU capacity reporting ensures pods with CPU requests are scheduled correctly and prevents over‑commit or under‑utilization on nodes using the CPU manager.

bugOrRegression.description: Pod logs using --timestamps are not broken up with timestamps anymore.
bugOrRegression.author: rphillips

enrichment.problem: When using `kubectl logs --timestamps`, the log output no longer splits logs with timestamps per line, resulting in unreadable or concatenated timestamps.
enrichment.affected: Users who retrieve pod logs with the `--timestamps` flag (e.g., via `kubectl logs`).
enrichment.fix: Adjusted the logging machinery so that each log line is correctly prefixed with its own timestamp when the `--timestamps` flag is used.
enrichment.impact: Restores accurate per‑line timestamps in pod logs, enabling reliable debugging and log analysis for users who depend on timestamped output.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix endpoint reconciler not being able to delete the apiserver lease on shutdown
bugOrRegression.author: aojea

enrichment.affected: Clusters running multiple kube-apiserver replicas (HA setups) could retain a stale lease after a node or apiserver shutdown, affecting leader election.
enrichment.fix: The shutdown path now correctly removes the apiserver lease via the endpoint reconciler, ensuring the lease is cleaned up during graceful termination.
enrichment.impact: Prevents stale leases that can block or confuse leader election in HA API server deployments, improving reliability of failover and reducing the chance of split‑brain scenarios.

bugOrRegression.description: Resolves an issue that causes winkernel proxier to treat stale VIPs as valid
bugOrRegression.author: daschott

enrichment.problem: The winkernel proxier on Windows nodes incorrectly considered stale virtual IPs (VIPs) as still valid, leading to traffic being sent to outdated or non-existent service endpoints.
enrichment.affected: Windows nodes running kube-proxy in winkernel mode; services that rely on VIPs for load balancing.
enrichment.fix: The proxier logic was updated to properly detect and discard stale VIPs, ensuring only current, healthy VIPs are used for routing.
enrichment.impact: Prevents misrouting of service traffic on Windows clusters, improving reliability and correctness of load‑balancing for services that use VIPs.

bugOrRegression.description: Updates golang.org/x/net to fix CVE-2022-41717
bugOrRegression.author: liggitt

enrichment.fix: The release updates golang.org/x/net to a version that patches CVE-2022-41717 and rebuilds all affected binaries.
enrichment.impact: Eliminates a security risk across the cluster, protecting components that use the Go net library from potential remote attacks or denial‑of‑service conditions.
