bugOrRegression.description: Client-go: fixes potential data races retrying requests using a custom io.Reader body; with this fix, only requests with no body or with string / []byte / runtime.Object bodies can be retried
bugOrRegression.author: liggitt

enrichment.problem: client-go could experience data races when retrying HTTP requests that used a custom io.Reader as the request body, leading to potential corruption or crashes.
enrichment.affected: Any component or controller that uses client-go with custom io.Reader request bodies and relies on automatic request retries (e.g., controllers, kubectl, custom operators).
enrichment.fix: The retry logic is updated to only allow retries for requests with no body or bodies that are safe to replay (string, []byte, or runtime.Object). Custom io.Reader bodies are no longer retried.
enrichment.impact: Prevents rare but serious race conditions in components that rely on client-go retries, improving stability and correctness of API interactions.

bugOrRegression.description: Do not include preemptor pod metadata in the event message
bugOrRegression.author: mimowo

enrichment.problem: Event messages for preempted pods included metadata from the preemptor pod, leading to noisy or overly detailed event data.
enrichment.affected: Users and tools that monitor Kubernetes events, especially those tracking pod preemptions, were seeing unnecessary preemptor pod details.
enrichment.fix: The scheduler now omits preemptor pod metadata when generating preemption event messages, showing only the relevant information about the preempted pod.
enrichment.impact: Users receive cleaner, more relevant preemption events, improving observability and reducing accidental exposure of unrelated pod details.

bugOrRegression.description: Failed pods associated with a job with `parallelism = 1` are recreated by the job controller honoring exponential backoff delay again. However, for jobs with `parallelism > 1`, pods might be created without exponential backoff delay.
bugOrRegression.author: nikhita

enrichment.problem: For Job objects with parallelism > 1, failed pods were sometimes recreated immediately without applying the exponential backoff delay, leading to rapid pod restart loops.
enrichment.affected: Jobs that specify parallelism greater than 1; their failed pods could be recreated without backoff, potentially flooding the cluster with rapid restarts.
enrichment.fix: The job controller now applies the exponential backoff algorithm for all failed pods regardless of the Job's parallelism setting, ensuring consistent backoff behavior.
enrichment.impact: Prevents pod thrashing and reduces unnecessary API/server load for Jobs with multiple parallel pods, improving workload stability and respecting user‑defined backoff policies.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix a regression that the scheduler always goes through all Filter plugins.
bugOrRegression.author: Huang-Wei

enrichment.problem: A regression caused the kube-scheduler to invoke every Filter plugin for each scheduling attempt, even when earlier plugins already rejected the pod, leading to unnecessary CPU work and higher scheduling latency.
enrichment.affected: All clusters that rely on the scheduler, particularly those using custom or multiple Filter plugins, experienced slower scheduling due to the regression.
enrichment.fix: The scheduler logic was corrected so that it stops evaluating Filter plugins as soon as a plugin returns a failure, restoring the intended short‑circuit behavior.
enrichment.impact: Scheduling latency is reduced and CPU consumption of the scheduler drops, especially in clusters with many or expensive Filter plugins. This improves overall cluster performance and responsiveness.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix bug in CRD Validation Rules (beta) and ValidatingAdmissionPolicy (alpha) where all admission requests could result in `internal error: runtime error: index out of range [3] with length 3 evaluating rule: <rule name>` under certain circumstances.
bugOrRegression.author: jpbetz

enrichment.problem: When using CRD Validation Rules (beta) or ValidatingAdmissionPolicy (alpha), certain admission requests could trigger a panic in the API server, resulting in `internal error: runtime error: index out of range [3] with length 3 evaluating rule: <rule name>`.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that have CRD Validation Rules (beta) or ValidatingAdmissionPolicy (alpha) enabled; any user creating or updating resources that rely on those validation mechanisms.
enrichment.fix: The evaluation logic for CRD validation rules and validating admission policies was fixed to correctly handle edge‑case indices, preventing the out‑of‑range panic and allowing admission requests to be processed normally.
enrichment.impact: Admission requests that depended on these validation rules would fail with an internal server error, breaking creation or update of CRDs and workloads that use ValidatingAdmissionPolicy, leading to service disruption for clusters using these features.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed DaemonSet to update the status even if it fails to create a pod.
bugOrRegression.author: gjkim42

enrichment.problem: When a DaemonSet failed to create a pod, the DaemonSet controller did not update the DaemonSet status, causing the status to be out‑of‑sync with reality.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using DaemonSet workloads; operators relying on DaemonSet status for health checks or automation.
enrichment.fix: The DaemonSet controller now always updates the DaemonSet status, even if pod creation fails, ensuring the status reflects the actual outcome of the rollout attempt.
enrichment.impact: Users and operators get accurate status information for DaemonSets, making troubleshooting and monitoring easier and preventing misleading readiness reports.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixing issue in Winkernel Proxier - Unexpected active TCP connection drops while horizontally scaling the endpoints for a LoadBalancer Service with External Traffic Policy: Local
bugOrRegression.author: princepereira

enrichment.problem: Active TCP connections were unintentionally dropped when the set of endpoints for a LoadBalancer Service with externalTrafficPolicy=Local was scaled horizontally on Windows nodes using the winkernel proxier.
enrichment.affected: Users running Windows nodes that expose LoadBalancer Services with externalTrafficPolicy=Local; specifically, active TCP sessions could be dropped during endpoint scaling.
enrichment.fix: The winkernel proxier logic was updated to correctly handle endpoint changes without resetting existing connections, preventing premature connection termination during scaling operations.
enrichment.impact: LoadBalancer services with externalTrafficPolicy=Local on Windows clusters now maintain stable TCP connections during scaling, improving service reliability and preventing unexpected client disruptions.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixing issue with Winkernel Proxier - No ingress load balancer rules with endpoints to support load balancing when all the endpoints are terminating.
bugOrRegression.author: princepereira

enrichment.problem: When using the Winkernel Proxier (kube-proxy in Windows mode), no ingress load balancer rules were generated if all service endpoints were in a terminating state, causing loss of traffic to those services.
enrichment.affected: Windows nodes running kube-proxy in winkernel mode; services/Ingress resources whose endpoints become terminating.
enrichment.fix: Implemented logic to create and maintain ingress load balancer rules even when all endpoints are terminating, ensuring proper load‑balancing behavior for Windows services.
enrichment.impact: Prevents service disruption for Windows workloads that temporarily have only terminating endpoints, ensuring continuous traffic routing and reliability of ingress/LoadBalancer services.

bugOrRegression.description: Kubelet: make the image pull time more accurate in event
bugOrRegression.author: pacoxu

enrichment.problem: Kubelet events reported inaccurate image pull durations, making it hard for users to diagnose slow image pulls.
enrichment.affected: Users and operators relying on kubelet events to monitor image pull times for pods.
enrichment.fix: Kubelet now records the start and end timestamps of image pulls more precisely, resulting in events that reflect the true pull time.
enrichment.impact: Provides more accurate observability for image pull performance, helping operators and developers troubleshoot pod startup delays.

bugOrRegression.description: Optimizing loadbalancer creation with the help of attribute Internal Traffic Policy: Local
bugOrRegression.author: princepereira

enrichment.problem: Creating Services of type LoadBalancer could be inefficient, especially when using internal traffic policies, leading to slower provisioning and unnecessary resource usage.
enrichment.affected: Users who create LoadBalancer Services with internal traffic routing; clusters using the Service controller (cloud-controller-manager) for load balancer provisioning.
enrichment.fix: Introduce and leverage the `internalTrafficPolicy: Local` attribute during LoadBalancer Service creation, allowing the controller to optimize the provisioning process.
enrichment.impact: LoadBalancer services are created faster and with fewer resources, improving cluster performance and reducing cost for workloads that use internal traffic routing.

bugOrRegression.description: Update the system-validators library to v1.8.0
bugOrRegression.author: pacoxu

enrichment.problem: The cluster used an older version of the system-validators library, which could miss newer validation rules or contain bugs fixed in later releases.
enrichment.affected: All control‑plane components and kubelet that rely on system-validators for request validation (e.g., kube-apiserver, scheduler, controller‑manager, kubelet).
enrichment.fix: The system-validators library is upgraded to v1.8.0, bringing the latest validation logic and bug fixes into the control plane and node components.
enrichment.impact: Improves the accuracy of resource validation across the cluster, reducing chances of invalid objects being accepted and preventing downstream errors.

feature.description:
Kubelet TCP and HTTP probes are more effective using networking resources: conntrack entries, sockets, ... 
  This is achieved by reducing the TIME-WAIT state of the connection to 1 second, instead of the defaults 60 seconds. This allows kubelet to free the socket, and free conntrack entry and ephemeral port associated.
feature.author: aojea

enrichment.problem: Kubelet TCP and HTTP readiness/liveness probes left connections in the TIME-WAIT state for the default 60 seconds, exhausting sockets, conntrack entries, and ephemeral ports on nodes with many probes.
enrichment.affected: Nodes running kubelet with many TCP/HTTP probes, especially large clusters or workloads with frequent health checks.
enrichment.fix: Kubelet now reduces the TIME-WAIT duration to 1 second for probe connections, allowing sockets, conntrack entries, and ports to be reclaimed promptly.
enrichment.impact: Probe reliability improves and node networking resources are preserved, preventing probe failures and service disruptions in high‑pod‑density clusters.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with Go 1.19.6
feature.author: cpanato

enrichment.problem: The Kubernetes binaries were previously built with an older Go version, which could miss upstream security fixes and runtime improvements.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes components (kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, kube-controller-manager, kubelet, kube-proxy, kubectl, etc.) built from source for this release.
enrichment.fix: All Kubernetes components are now compiled with Go 1.19.6, incorporating the latest language runtime patches and compiler enhancements.
enrichment.impact: Users receive binaries that benefit from Go's security patches, performance improvements, and bug fixes, reducing potential runtime issues and aligning with the supported Go version for future development.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix a bug that caused to panic the apiserver when trying to allocate a Service with a dynamic ClusterIP and it has been configured with Service CIDRs with a /28 mask for IPv4 and a /124 mask for IPv6
bugOrRegression.author: aojea

enrichment.problem: kube-apiserver would panic and crash when allocating a Service with a dynamic ClusterIP if the cluster’s Service CIDR used a very small subnet mask (/28 for IPv4 or /124 for IPv6).
enrichment.affected: Cluster administrators and workloads that create Services with dynamic ClusterIPs in clusters configured with Service CIDRs of /28 IPv4 or /124 IPv6.
enrichment.fix: Adjusted the Service CIDR validation and IP allocation logic so that small CIDR masks are handled correctly, preventing the apiserver panic during Service creation.
enrichment.impact: The control plane remains stable when creating Services in clusters that use small Service CIDR ranges, allowing use of /28 IPv4 or /124 IPv6 subnets without risking a server crash.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix nil pointer error in nodevolumelimits csi logging
bugOrRegression.author: sunnylovestiramisu

enrichment.problem: A nil pointer dereference could occur in the nodevolumelimits scheduling plugin when logging CSI volume information, causing the kube-scheduler to panic.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that enable the NodeVolumeLimits scheduler plugin (used for CSI volume limits) could experience scheduler crashes due to the nil pointer bug.
enrichment.fix: Added defensive checks in the nodevolumelimits CSI logging code to ensure pointers are non‑nil before accessing them, preventing the panic.
enrichment.impact: Prevents scheduler crashes for clusters that use the NodeVolumeLimits plugin with CSI volumes, improving overall cluster stability and availability.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix the regression that introduced 34s timeout for DELETECOLLECTION calls
bugOrRegression.author: tkashem

enrichment.problem: A regression introduced an unintended 34‑second timeout for DELETECOLLECTION API calls, causing bulk delete operations to fail or be delayed.
enrichment.affected: Clients and controllers that rely on DELETECOLLECTION to remove multiple resources at once experienced failures or long waits.
enrichment.fix: The regression was fixed by restoring the correct timeout handling for DELETECOLLECTION requests, allowing them to complete without the excessive delay.
enrichment.impact: Bulk delete operations (e.g., `kubectl delete -A`, controller garbage collection) work as expected again, preventing unnecessary errors and improving API responsiveness.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed bug which caused the status of Indexed Jobs to only be updated when there are newly completed indexes. The completed indexes are now updated if the .status.completedIndexes has values outside of the [0, .spec.completions> range
bugOrRegression.author: danielvegamyhre

enrichment.problem: The status of Indexed Jobs was only refreshed when new indexes completed. If .status.completedIndexes contained values outside the valid range (0 to .spec.completions‑1), the status was not updated, leading to stale or inaccurate job status.
enrichment.affected: Users employing Indexed Jobs (jobs with .spec.completionMode=Indexed) whose completedIndexes could be set outside the normal range.
enrichment.fix: Job controller logic was adjusted to always update the .status.completedIndexes field, regardless of whether the values fall outside the expected range, ensuring the job status reflects the actual completed indexes.
enrichment.impact: Users running Indexed Jobs now see correct status information, which improves observability and prevents confusion in monitoring or automation that relies on completedIndexes.

bugOrRegression.description: Golang.org/x/net updates to v0.7.0 to fix CVE-2022-41723
bugOrRegression.author: liggitt

enrichment.problem: A vulnerability (CVE-2022-41723) in the golang.org/x/net library could be exploited via crafted HTTP/2 traffic to cause a denial‑of‑service, potentially disrupting Kubernetes components that use this library.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes binaries that link against golang.org/x/net (e.g., kube-apiserver, kubelet, kube-proxy, kube-controller-manager, kube-scheduler, kubectl) were vulnerable to the issue.
enrichment.fix: The golang.org/x/net dependency is updated to version v0.7.0, which contains the patch that mitigates CVE-2022-41723.
enrichment.impact: Removes the DoS attack surface across the control plane and client tools, improving overall cluster reliability and security.

bugOrRegression.description: The Kubernetes API server now correctly detects and closes existing TLS connections when its client certificate file for kubelet authentication has been rotated.
bugOrRegression.author: enj

enrichment.problem: The API server did not detect that its client certificate file used for kubelet authentication had been rotated, so existing TLS connections remained open and continued using the old certificate, leading to authentication failures for kubelets after a cert rotation.
enrichment.affected: Clusters where kubelet client certificates are rotated; affected nodes may temporarily lose API access until the bug is fixed.
enrichment.fix: The kube-apiserver now watches the client certificate file for kubelet authentication and, when the file changes, it proactively closes any existing TLS connections that were established with the previous certificate, forcing a new handshake with the updated cert.
enrichment.impact: Node kubelet components can reliably rotate their client certificates without losing connectivity to the API server, preventing temporary node‑health issues and reducing operational friction during security credential rotation.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with Go 1.19.7
feature.author: cpanato

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes binaries were previously built with an older Go version, which could miss security patches and performance improvements.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes components compiled from source (kubelet, kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, controller-manager, kubectl, kube-proxy, etc.)
enrichment.fix: The build process has been updated to use Go 1.19.7 for compiling all Kubernetes components.
enrichment.impact: Upgrading the Go toolchain brings in upstream security fixes, bug fixes, and performance enhancements, ensuring the binaries remain supported and reduce potential supply‑chain risks.

feature.description: The go version defined in `.go-version` is now fetched when invoking test, build, and code generation targets if the current go version does not match it. Set $FORCE_HOST_GO=y while testing or building to skip this behavior, or set $GO_VERSION to override the selected go version.
feature.author: liggitt

enrichment.problem: When invoking test, build, or code generation Make targets, the go version used could differ from the version specified in the repository's .go-version file, leading to build failures or inconsistent behavior.
enrichment.affected: Developers running `make test`, `make build`, or code generation targets, as well as CI systems that rely on these targets.
enrichment.fix: The make logic now automatically fetches and uses the go version defined in .go-version if the host's go version does not match. Users can bypass this by setting FORCE_HOST_GO=y or override the selected version with GO_VERSION.
enrichment.impact: Developers and CI pipelines get reproducible builds and test runs without manually managing the go version, reducing friction and build errors.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix data race in kube-scheduler when preemption races with a Pod update.
bugOrRegression.author: alculquicondor

enrichment.problem: A data race in kube-scheduler could occur when a preemption operation happened at the same time as a Pod update, leading to inconsistent scheduling state or incorrect preemption decisions.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using preemption (e.g., with PriorityClasses) where Pods are frequently updated, potentially causing scheduling inconsistencies.
enrichment.fix: The scheduler code was updated to synchronize access to shared data structures during preemption and Pod updates, eliminating the race condition.
enrichment.impact: Ensures reliable preemption handling and accurate scheduling decisions, preventing missed preemptions or unexpected pod evictions in clusters with frequent pod updates.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix log line in scheduler that inaccurately implies that volume binding has finalized
bugOrRegression.author: TommyStarK

enrichment.problem: The scheduler emitted a log line that incorrectly suggested volume binding had already completed, which could mislead users during troubleshooting.
enrichment.affected: Cluster operators and developers who read scheduler logs to understand volume binding progress.
enrichment.fix: The log message has been corrected to accurately reflect the state of volume binding, removing the implication that it is finalized.
enrichment.impact: Improves log clarity, preventing confusion for administrators and developers when diagnosing scheduling and volume binding issues.

bugOrRegression.description:
Fixed a bug where Kubernetes would apply a default StorageClass to a PersistentVolumeClaim,
  even when the deprecated annotation `volume.beta.kubernetes.io/storage-class` was set.
bugOrRegression.author: cvvz

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes incorrectly applied the cluster's default StorageClass to a PersistentVolumeClaim even when the deprecated annotation `volume.beta.kubernetes.io/storage-class` was set, causing the PVC to use the wrong storage class.
enrichment.affected: Users creating PersistentVolumeClaims that include the `volume.beta.kubernetes.io/storage-class` annotation; workloads that rely on that annotation for storage class selection.
enrichment.fix: The admission logic now respects the deprecated storage‑class annotation and skips default‑StorageClass assignment when the annotation is present.
enrichment.impact: PVCs created with the deprecated annotation will receive the intended storage class, preventing unexpected volume provisioning and maintaining compatibility for workloads that still use the annotation.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixing issue with Winkernel Proxier - ClusterIP Loadbalancers are missing if the ExternalTrafficPolicy is set to Local and the available endpoints are all remoteEndpoints.
bugOrRegression.author: princepereira

enrichment.problem: When using the winkernel proxier on Windows nodes, services of type ClusterIP with externalTrafficPolicy=Local did not create load balancer entries if all endpoints were remote, causing traffic to be dropped.
enrichment.affected: Windows nodes using the winkernel proxier and any Service with externalTrafficPolicy=Local where all endpoints reside on other nodes.
enrichment.fix: The winkernel proxier logic was updated to generate the necessary load balancer entries even when the only available endpoints are remote, ensuring the service remains reachable.
enrichment.impact: Windows workloads that rely on ClusterIP services with externalTrafficPolicy=Local now receive traffic correctly, preventing service outages and improving reliability of Windows networking in mixed‑node clusters.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixing issue with Winkernel Proxier - IPV6 load balancer policies are missing when service is configured with ipFamilyPolicy: RequireDualStack
bugOrRegression.author: princepereira

enrichment.problem: When a Service is configured with ipFamilyPolicy=RequireDualStack, the winkernel proxier (Windows kube-proxy) fails to create IPv6 load balancer policies, causing IPv6 traffic to be dropped or not load‑balanced.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using Windows nodes with the winkernel proxier and Services configured with ipFamilyPolicy=RequireDualStack.
enrichment.fix: The winkernel proxier now correctly generates IPv6 load balancer policies for Services that require dual‑stack, ensuring both IPv4 and IPv6 traffic are handled.
enrichment.impact: Restores proper load‑balancing of IPv6 traffic on dual‑stack Services for Windows nodes, preventing loss of connectivity and improving reliability of mixed‑stack workloads.

bugOrRegression.description: Make kubectl diff --prune behave correctly with the --selector/-l flag
bugOrRegression.author: nathanmartins

enrichment.problem: When using 'kubectl diff' with the '--prune' flag together with '--selector' (or '-l'), the selector was ignored, resulting in incorrect diff output that included resources outside the selector scope.
enrichment.affected: kubectl users who run 'kubectl diff' with both '--prune' and '--selector'/'-l' flags.
enrichment.fix: The command now correctly applies the label selector while pruning, limiting the diff to only those resources that match the selector.
enrichment.impact: Users get accurate diff results when filtering resources, avoiding confusion and accidental changes. Improves reliability of 'kubectl diff' in CI/CD and troubleshooting workflows.

bugOrRegression.description: Remove check for CSI driver running on node for CSI migration
bugOrRegression.author: sunnylovestiramisu

enrichment.problem: Kubelet performed a check to verify that a CSI driver was running on the node before allowing CSI migration. In clusters where the driver was not yet deployed on every node (e.g., during migration or rolling upgrades), this check caused pod startup failures and blocked migration of in‑tree volume plugins to CSI.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that enable CSI migration for in‑tree volume plugins, especially those where the CSI driver is not present on every node at migration time, could experience pod scheduling failures. The change targets these scenarios.
enrichment.fix: The node‑level CSI driver presence check has been removed from kubelet. Migration now proceeds without requiring the driver to be running on each node, allowing pods that use migrated volumes to start successfully.
enrichment.impact: Users performing CSI migration will see fewer pod‑startup errors and smoother migration of in‑tree storage plugins to external CSI drivers. It reduces operational friction during rolling upgrades or when drivers are deployed as DaemonSets after workloads are already running.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with Go 1.19.8
feature.author: xmudrii

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes builds were using an older Go version, which may lack recent security patches, bug fixes, and performance improvements.
enrichment.affected: Any environment that builds Kubernetes from source, including CI/CD pipelines and custom builds of all control‑plane and node components.
enrichment.fix: The build process has been updated to compile all Kubernetes components with Go 1.19.8.
enrichment.impact: All Kubernetes binaries now benefit from the latest Go runtime fixes and optimizations, improving overall stability, security, and compatibility for downstream users and CI pipelines.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix missing delete events on informer re-lists to ensure all delete events are correctly emitted and using the latest known object state, so that all event handlers and stores always reflect the actual apiserver state as best as possible
bugOrRegression.author: odinuge

enrichment.problem: During informer re-list operations, delete events were not emitted for objects that disappeared, causing event handlers and stores to become out of sync with the apiserver state.
enrichment.affected: Any component or custom controller that uses client-go informers (e.g., controller-runtime, operators) could miss delete events, leading to inconsistent view of resources.
enrichment.fix: The informer now generates delete events for missing objects on re-list, using the latest known object state, ensuring all handlers receive accurate delete notifications.
enrichment.impact: Controllers, operators, and any code that relies on informers will see correct object lifecycle events, preventing stale state and related bugs.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix: Route controller should update routes with NodeIP changed
bugOrRegression.author: lzhecheng

enrichment.problem: The route controller did not update cloud routes when a node's IP address changed, leaving stale routes in the cloud provider.
enrichment.affected: Kubernetes clusters using the cloud provider route controller; nodes whose IP changes; workloads that rely on correct cloud routing.
enrichment.fix: The controller now watches for NodeIP changes and updates the corresponding cloud routes to reflect the new IP address.
enrichment.impact: Nodes that receive a new IP (e.g., after reboot or DHCP renewal) will maintain correct routing, preventing loss of network connectivity for pods and services that depend on cloud routes.

bugOrRegression.description:
Fixes a regression in the pod binding subresource to honor the `metadata.uid` precondition.
  This allows kube-scheduler to ensure it is assigns node names to the same instances of pods it made scheduling decisions for.
bugOrRegression.author: alculquicondor

enrichment.problem: A regression caused the pod binding subresource to ignore the metadata.uid precondition, allowing the scheduler to bind a node name to a different pod instance than the one it scheduled.
enrichment.affected: Clusters where pods are scheduled could experience pods being bound to the wrong instance, leading to scheduling errors or pods remaining unscheduled.
enrichment.fix: The pod binding logic was updated to honor the metadata.uid precondition, ensuring the kube-scheduler only binds the exact pod instance it made scheduling decisions for.
enrichment.impact: Prevents incorrect pod bindings and scheduling failures, improving reliability of pod placement and avoiding potential disruptions for workloads.

bugOrRegression.description: Kubelet: Fix fs quota monitoring on volumes
bugOrRegression.author: pacoxu

enrichment.problem: Kubelet failed to correctly monitor filesystem quota usage on mounted volumes, leading to inaccurate quota metrics and potential over-consumption of storage by pods.
enrichment.affected: Any pod that uses a volume with filesystem quota enabled on nodes running the affected kubelet version.
enrichment.fix: Implemented proper filesystem quota monitoring in the kubelet for all volume types, ensuring accurate tracking and enforcement of quota limits.
enrichment.impact: Provides reliable quota enforcement, preventing pods from exceeding allocated storage and improving node stability and storage management for users relying on quota‑based volume usage.

other.description: Service session affinity timeout tests are no longer required for Kubernetes network plugin conformance due to variations in existing implementations. New conformance tests will be developed to better express conformance in future releases.
other.author: dcbw

enrichment.problem: Service session affinity timeout tests were required for network plugin conformance, but existing implementations vary, causing inconsistent test results.
enrichment.affected: Network plugin developers and users running conformance tests; also clusters relying on Service session affinity behavior.
enrichment.fix: The affinity timeout tests have been removed from the required conformance suite. New, more expressive conformance tests will be added in future releases.
enrichment.impact: Reduces false negatives in conformance testing for network plugins, easing the testing process for developers and operators. Future tests will provide clearer conformance criteria.

apiChange.description: Added error handling for seccomp localhost configurations that do not properly set a localhostProfile
apiChange.author: cji

enrichment.problem: Pods that specify a seccomp profile via a localhostProfile can fail to start or run without the intended profile when the configuration does not correctly set the localhostProfile, leading to silent security gaps or errors.
enrichment.affected: Users who use custom seccomp localhost profiles in pod specifications. Workloads that rely on those profiles may have failed or run without proper syscall filtering.
enrichment.fix: Added validation and error handling in the node component to detect missing or malformed localhostProfile entries for seccomp and report a clear error instead of proceeding with an undefined profile.
enrichment.impact: Improves cluster reliability and security posture by preventing pods from running with unintended or missing seccomp restrictions and gives users immediate feedback to correct their configuration.

apiChange.description: Fixed an issue where kubelet does not set case-insensitive headers for http probes. (#117182, @dddddai)
apiChange.author: dddddai

enrichment.problem: kubelet sent HTTP probe headers with case-sensitive handling, violating the HTTP spec that header names are case‑insensitive, causing health‑check probes to fail when the target service expected a different case.
enrichment.affected: Pods that define HTTP liveness or readiness probes relying on case‑insensitive header matching could experience false failures; the issue affected the kubelet component that performs the probes.
enrichment.fix: kubelet now normalizes probe headers to be case‑insensitive (e.g., lower‑casing header names) before sending HTTP liveness/readiness probes.
enrichment.impact: Probes succeed as intended, preventing unnecessary pod restarts or failures caused by header‑case mismatches, improving reliability of liveness/readiness checks for workloads that use HTTP probes.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with Go 1.19.9
feature.author: xmudrii

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes binaries were built with an older Go version, which could miss upstream Go security patches and future language improvements.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes binaries (kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, kube-controller-manager, kubelet, kube-proxy, kubectl, etc.) are rebuilt with Go 1.19.9.
enrichment.fix: All Kubernetes components are now compiled with Go 1.19.9, bringing the project up to date with the latest Go release and its bug/security fixes.
enrichment.impact: Provides security, performance, and stability improvements from the newer Go runtime to all Kubernetes components, and aligns the codebase with the current upstream Go release for future development.

enrichment.problem: Three high‑impact vulnerabilities (CVE‑2023‑27561, CVE‑2023‑25809, CVE‑2023‑28642) in runc 1.1.4 could allow container escape or privilege escalation.
enrichment.affected: Any node using the built‑in runc (via kubelet) with version 1.1.4 or earlier; workloads running containers on those nodes.
enrichment.fix: Kubernetes now bundles runc 1.1.5, which contains patches for the three CVEs.
enrichment.impact: Clusters that run containers with the vulnerable runc version are no longer exposed to the exploits, improving cluster security.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixes a problem of cgroup removal when using runc binary >= 1.1.6 (#117647)
bugOrRegression.author: kolyshkin

enrichment.problem: When using runc version 1.1.6 or newer, kubelet incorrectly removed cgroup directories, leading to loss of cgroup state for containers.
enrichment.affected: Nodes running kubelet with the runc container runtime version 1.1.6 or newer; pods on those nodes could experience disrupted cgroup management.
enrichment.fix: The kubelet code was updated to detect runc >=1.1.6 and avoid the faulty cgroup removal path, preserving cgroup hierarchy for running pods.
enrichment.impact: Prevents pods from losing their cgroup tracking, ensuring correct resource accounting and stable container lifecycle on affected nodes.

bugOrRegression.description: During device plugin allocation, resources requested by the pod can only be allocated if the device plugin has registered itself to kubelet AND healthy devices are present on the node to be allocated. If these conditions are not sattsfied, the pod would fail with `UnexpectedAdmissionError` error.
bugOrRegression.author: swatisehgal

enrichment.problem: Pods that request device plugin resources could be admitted even when the device plugin was not registered with the kubelet or when no healthy devices existed on the node, resulting in pod creation failures with an UnexpectedAdmissionError.
enrichment.affected: Workloads that request device plugin resources on nodes where the plugin is unregistered or has no healthy devices.
enrichment.fix: Kubelet now validates that a device plugin is registered and that healthy devices are available before allocating resources. If either condition is missing, the allocation is blocked and the pod is rejected with a clear admission error rather than an UnexpectedAdmissionError.
enrichment.impact: Pods relying on device plugins (e.g., GPUs, FPGAs) will no longer encounter obscure admission failures, providing more predictable scheduling and clearer error reporting for users.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix incorrect calculation for ResourceQuota with PriorityClass as its scope.
bugOrRegression.author: Huang-Wei

enrichment.problem: ResourceQuota objects scoped to a PriorityClass were calculated incorrectly, leading to inaccurate quota accounting.
enrichment.affected: Cluster administrators and workloads that rely on ResourceQuota scoped to a PriorityClass could see incorrect quota enforcement.
enrichment.fix: Adjusted the quota calculation logic in the API server to correctly account for resources when a ResourceQuota is scoped by PriorityClass.
enrichment.impact: Ensures that ResourceQuota enforcement works as expected for priority‑class scoped quotas, preventing unexpected resource overallocation or denial of pod creation.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix: the volume is not detached after the pod and PVC objects are deleted
bugOrRegression.author: cvvz

enrichment.problem: When a Pod and its associated PersistentVolumeClaim (PVC) are deleted, the attached volume is not detached, leaving stale volume attachments on the node.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using CSI or other volume plugins where Pods with PVCs are deleted; any workload that expects automatic volume cleanup after deletion.
enrichment.fix: Added logic to ensure that volume detach operations are triggered after pod and PVC deletion, cleaning up the attachment state correctly.
enrichment.impact: Prevents volume attachment leaks, allowing volumes to be re‑used and avoiding attach limits or potential errors for subsequent Pods. Improves reliability for workloads that frequently create and delete PVC‑backed Pods.

bugOrRegression.description: Number of errors reported to the metric `storage_operation_duration_seconds_count` for emptyDir decreased significantly because previously one error was reported for each projected volume created.
bugOrRegression.author: mpatlasov

enrichment.problem: The metric `storage_operation_duration_seconds_count` was incremented for every projected volume created when using emptyDir, causing a large number of spurious error counts.
enrichment.affected: Users and operators who rely on storage operation duration metrics for emptyDir volumes, especially those with alerts based on error counts.
enrichment.fix: The volume handling code was updated so that an error is only recorded for genuine storage operation failures, not for each projected volume creation with emptyDir.
enrichment.impact: Metrics for emptyDir storage operations are now accurate, reducing false positives in monitoring and alerting systems and improving observability of actual storage issues.

bugOrRegression.description: Setting a mirror pod's phase to Succeeded or Failed can prevent the corresponding static pod from restarting due mutation of a Kubelet cache.
bugOrRegression.author: smarterclayton

enrichment.problem: When the kubelet sets the phase of a mirror pod to Succeeded or Failed, it mutates the kubelet cache in a way that can stop the associated static pod from being restarted.
enrichment.affected: Clusters running static pods managed by the kubelet; nodes where static pods need to be restarted after a phase change were affected.
enrichment.fix: The kubelet logic was updated to avoid mutating the cache when updating a mirror pod's phase, ensuring that static pods can be correctly restarted after a phase change.
enrichment.impact: Static pods (e.g., self‑hosted control‑plane components) will no longer get stuck and fail to restart, improving node reliability and uptime.

other.description: A v2-level info log will be added, which will output the details of the pod being preempted, including victim and preemptor
other.author: HirazawaUi

enrichment.problem: Preemption events in the scheduler lacked detailed logs, making it hard for admins to see which pod was preempted (victim) and which pod caused the preemption (preemptor).
enrichment.affected: Cluster administrators and developers troubleshooting pod preemption scenarios.
enrichment.fix: Adds a v2-level info log entry that includes the victim and preemptor pod details whenever a pod is preempted by the scheduler.
enrichment.impact: Improves observability and debugging of scheduling preemptions, helping operators diagnose and understand why pods are being evicted.

securityFixes.title: Bypassing enforce mountable secrets policy imposed by the ServiceAccount admission plugin
securityFixes.description:
A security issue was discovered in Kubernetes where users may be able to launch containers that bypass the mountable secrets policy enforced by the ServiceAccount admission plugin when using ephemeral containers. The policy ensures pods running with a service account may only reference secrets specified in the service account's secrets field. Kubernetes clusters are only affected if the ServiceAccount admission plugin and the `kubernetes.io/enforce-mountable-secrets` annotation are used together with ephemeral containers.

**Note**: This only impacts the cluster if the ServiceAccount admission plugin is used (most cluster should have this on by default as recommended in https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/access-authn-authz/admission-controllers/#serviceaccount), the `kubernetes.io/enforce-mountable-secrets` annotation is used by a service account (this annotation is not added by default), and Pods are using ephemeral containers.

feature.description: Kubernetes 1.25.x is now built with Go 1.19.10
feature.author: puerco

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes 1.25.x releases were previously built with an older Go version, limiting access to newer language features, compiler optimizations, and security fixes.
enrichment.affected: All clusters running Kubernetes 1.25.x, since every component (kube-apiserver, kube-controller-manager, kube-scheduler, kubelet, kubectl, etc.) is recompiled with Go 1.19.10.
enrichment.fix: The release is now built using Go 1.19.10, upgrading the compiler and standard library for all Kubernetes binaries.
enrichment.impact: All Kubernetes components rebuilt with the newer Go version benefit from improved performance, security patches, and bug fixes from the Go runtime, leading to more stable clusters and reduced exposure to known Go-level vulnerabilities.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixes a bug at kube-apiserver start where APIService objects for custom resources could be deleted and recreated.
bugOrRegression.author: liggitt

enrichment.problem: At kube-apiserver startup, APIService objects for aggregated custom resource APIs could be unintentionally deleted and then recreated, causing temporary loss of those APIs.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that use aggregated API servers (APIService objects) for custom resources; those APIs could become unavailable during apiserver restarts.
enrichment.fix: The start‑up logic of kube‑apiserver was updated to preserve existing APIService objects for custom resources, preventing their deletion and unnecessary recreation.
enrichment.impact: Custom resources served via aggregated API servers remain stable across apiserver restarts, avoiding brief outages and reducing the risk of client errors or data handling issues.

bugOrRegression.description: If `kubeadm reset` finds no etcd member ID for the peer it removes during the `remove-etcd-member` phase, it continues immediately to other phases, instead of retrying the phase for up to 3 minutes before continuing.
bugOrRegression.author: dlipovetsky

enrichment.problem: `kubeadm reset` skips the retry logic for the `remove-etcd-member` phase when it cannot find an etcd member ID for the peer, moving on to subsequent phases immediately.
enrichment.affected: Users invoking `kubeadm reset` on clusters where an etcd member ID is missing; scenarios where a node's etcd member has already been removed or is otherwise unavailable.
enrichment.fix: The reset process now correctly retries the `remove-etcd-member` phase for up to three minutes before proceeding, ensuring the removal attempt is given sufficient time.
enrichment.impact: Prevents incomplete etcd member removal during a cluster reset, reducing the risk of stale etcd entries and subsequent reset or upgrade failures.

bugOrRegression.description: Kubeadm: fix a bug where the static pod changes detection logic is inconsistent with kubelet
bugOrRegression.author: SataQiu

enrichment.problem: kubeadm's static pod change detection logic did not match the kubelet's logic, causing inconsistencies where updates to static pod manifests could be missed or incorrectly handled.
enrichment.affected: Clusters created with kubeadm that rely on static pod manifests for control‑plane components; the kubelet may have previously missed changes.
enrichment.fix: The detection algorithm in kubeadm was updated to use the same criteria as the kubelet, ensuring consistent detection of static pod changes.
enrichment.impact: Static pod updates (e.g., control‑plane component manifests) are now reliably detected and applied, preventing stale or out‑of‑sync control‑plane components and reducing operational issues for clusters bootstrapped with kubeadm.

feature.description: Kubernetes 1.25.x is now built with Go 1.20.5
feature.author: cpanato

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes 1.25.x releases were compiled with an older Go toolchain, which could miss upstream Go security patches, performance improvements, and language/runtime bug fixes.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes clusters running 1.25.x and anyone building from source; all binary components (kube-apiserver, kube-controller-manager, kube-scheduler, kubelet, kube-proxy, kubectl, etc.).
enrichment.fix: The release series is now built with Go 1.20.5, updating the compiler and runtime used for all Kubernetes binaries.
enrichment.impact: Users get binaries that include Go’s latest security fixes and performance enhancements, improving overall stability and reducing the risk of compiler‑related vulnerabilities. No functional changes to the cluster behavior are introduced.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with Go 1.20.6
feature.author: xmudrii

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes was previously built with an older Go version, which could cause build failures, missing security patches, and incompatibility with newer Go toolchains.
enrichment.affected: Anyone building Kubernetes from source, including CI systems and downstream vendors.
enrichment.fix: The build process has been updated to use Go 1.20.6, ensuring the codebase compiles with the latest supported Go release and incorporates upstream security and performance updates.
enrichment.impact: Developers, CI pipelines, and downstream distributors building Kubernetes from source will have a smoother build experience and benefit from the security and bug fixes in Go 1.20.6. No runtime behavior changes for clusters.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix component status calling etcd health endpoint over http which exposed kubernetes to the risk of complete watch starvation and is inconsistent with other etcd probing done by kube-apiserver.
bugOrRegression.author: serathius

enrichment.problem: ComponentStatus health checks queried the etcd health endpoint over HTTP, which could cause watch starvation and was inconsistent with the secure probing used by the kube-apiserver.
enrichment.affected: Clusters where the API server performed ComponentStatus checks over HTTP could experience watch starvation, affecting all workloads that rely on watch streams.
enrichment.fix: Updated the ComponentStatus health check to use the same TLS-secured etcd health endpoint as other kube-apiserver probes, eliminating the insecure HTTP call.
enrichment.impact: Prevents a scenario where the API server could become unresponsive to watch requests, improving cluster stability and aligning health checks with secure best‑practice behavior.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix cronjob controller handling of complex schedules, like "30 6-16/4 * * 1-5", for example
bugOrRegression.author: kmala

enrichment.problem: The cronjob controller mis‑handled complex cron schedule expressions (e.g., "30 6-16/4 * * 1-5"), leading to incorrect or missed job executions.
enrichment.affected: Users of CronJob resources that use complex cron schedule expressions.
enrichment.fix: Updated the cronjob controller logic in kube‑controller‑manager to correctly parse and evaluate complex cron schedules, ensuring jobs are created at the intended times.
enrichment.impact: CronJob workloads with advanced schedule syntax now run reliably, preventing missed runs or unintended extra executions, which improves workload reliability for users relying on precise scheduling.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed a performance issue where pods weren't created/deleted in parallel for a StatefulSet with podManagementPolicy: Parallel.
bugOrRegression.author: aleksandra-malinowska

enrichment.problem: When a StatefulSet is configured with podManagementPolicy: Parallel, the controller created and deleted pods sequentially instead of in parallel, causing slower scaling and rollout performance.
enrichment.affected: Users running StatefulSets with podManagementPolicy: Parallel, especially those with many replicas or frequent scaling events.
enrichment.fix: Updated the StatefulSet controller logic in kube-controller-manager to correctly handle parallel pod creation and deletion when podManagementPolicy is set to Parallel.
enrichment.impact: StatefulSet workloads that rely on parallel pod management now scale and roll out faster, reducing latency during scaling operations and improving overall performance for large StatefulSets.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed vSphere cloud provider not to skip detach volumes from nodes at kube-controller-startup.
bugOrRegression.author: jsafrane

enrichment.problem: When the kube-controller-manager started, the vSphere cloud provider incorrectly skipped detaching volumes from nodes, leaving volumes attached after they should have been detached.
enrichment.affected: Kubernetes clusters using the vSphere cloud provider, particularly when the controller manager restarts and volumes need to be detached from nodes.
enrichment.fix: The vSphere cloud provider logic was updated to ensure that volume detach operations are performed during kube-controller-manager startup, preventing orphaned volume attachments.
enrichment.impact: Prevents orphaned volume attachments that could cause storage capacity issues, node access errors, or failures to re‑attach volumes, improving cluster stability for vSphere users.

bugOrRegression.description: Kubeadm: explicitly set `priority` for static pods with `priorityClassName: system-node-critical`
bugOrRegression.author: champtar

enrichment.problem: Static pod manifests generated by kubeadm that set `priorityClassName: system-node-critical` did not set the corresponding `priority` field, causing those critical system pods to be treated with default priority and potentially be preempted or evicted.
enrichment.affected: Clusters provisioned with kubeadm that rely on static pods with `priorityClassName: system-node-critical`, such as control-plane components.
enrichment.fix: Kubeadm now explicitly writes the `priority` value into the static pod spec when `priorityClassName: system-node-critical` is used, ensuring the pod has the correct high priority.
enrichment.impact: Critical control-plane pods (e.g., etcd, kube-apiserver) run as static pods will retain their intended high priority, preventing unintended preemption or OOM eviction and improving cluster stability.

bugOrRegression.description: Only declare Job as finished after removing all Pod finalizers to avoid orphan Pods
bugOrRegression.author: alculquicondor

enrichment.problem: The Job controller could mark a Job as finished while its Pods still had finalizers, leaving those Pods orphaned after the Job was considered complete.
enrichment.affected: Users running batch Jobs that attach finalizers to Pods could see leftover Pods after the Job finished.
enrichment.fix: Job controller now waits until all Pod finalizers are removed before declaring the Job finished, ensuring proper pod cleanup.
enrichment.impact: Prevents orphaned Pods and resource leaks after Job completion, improving reliability of batch workloads and avoiding manual cleanup.

bugOrRegression.description: This PR adds additional validation for endpoint ip configuration while iterating through queried endpoint list.
bugOrRegression.author: princepereira

enrichment.problem: Endpoint objects could be created or updated with invalid IP configuration because the code did not fully validate IP fields while iterating the endpoint list, leading to potential networking errors especially on Windows clusters.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that create or update Service Endpoints with incorrect IP formats, notably Windows workloads that rely on strict IP validation.
enrichment.fix: Added comprehensive validation of endpoint IP configuration during iteration of the queried endpoint list, ensuring only well‑formed IPs are accepted.
enrichment.impact: Prevents malformed endpoint IP entries from being persisted, reducing network connectivity issues and improving reliability of Services and EndpointSlices, particularly on Windows nodes.

bugOrRegression.description: Updated cAdvisor to v0.45.1 - Fix metrics in cri-o when a container restarts
bugOrRegression.author: harche

enrichment.problem: cAdvisor produced incorrect or missing metrics for containers using the CRI-O runtime when those containers were restarted, leading to inaccurate observability data.
enrichment.affected: Clusters running the CRI-O container runtime on nodes where containers may be restarted; monitoring tools relying on cAdvisor metrics were affected.
enrichment.fix: Updated the bundled cAdvisor component to v0.45.1, which includes a fix to correctly handle and emit metrics for restarted CRI-O containers.
enrichment.impact: Node monitoring and alerting systems now receive accurate metrics for restarted containers, improving reliability of observability and troubleshooting for workloads using CRI-O.

securityFixes.title: Insufficient input sanitization on Windows nodes leads to privilege escalation
securityFixes.description: A security issue was discovered in Kubernetes where a user that can create pods on Windows nodes may be able to escalate to admin privileges on those nodes. Kubernetes clusters are only affected if they include Windows nodes.

securityFixes.title: Insufficient input sanitization on Windows nodes leads to privilege escalation
securityFixes.description: A security issue was discovered in Kubernetes where a user that can create pods on Windows nodes may be able to escalate to admin privileges on those nodes. Kubernetes clusters are only affected if they include Windows nodes.

feature.description:
Kubeadm: generate CA certificates with a start time that is offset 5 minutes in the past relative to the current system time to workaround cases of clock desync.
  client-go: allow to set NotBefore in NewSelfSignedCACert()
feature.author: champtar

enrichment.problem: When system clocks are out of sync, kubeadm-generated CA certificates had a NotBefore timestamp equal to the current time, causing the certificates to be considered not yet valid and breaking cluster bootstrap and any client-go code that generates self‑signed CAs.
enrichment.affected: Users initializing clusters with kubeadm or developers using client-go to create self‑signed CA certificates; environments where node clocks may drift.
enrichment.fix: Kubeadm now sets the NotBefore field of generated CA certificates to five minutes in the past. client-go’s NewSelfSignedCACert() was updated to allow callers to specify a custom NotBefore value, enabling the same workaround.
enrichment.impact: Clusters can be bootstrapped even if node clocks are a few minutes behind, preventing certificate‑validation errors during kubeadm init/join and reducing failure rates for setups with imperfect time synchronization.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with Go 1.20.7
feature.author: jeremyrickard

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes was built with an older Go toolchain, which can miss security patches, performance improvements, and may soon become unsupported.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes components (kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, kube-controller-manager, kubelet, kubectl, kube-proxy, etc.) are rebuilt with the newer Go version.
enrichment.fix: All Kubernetes binaries are now compiled with Go 1.20.7, updating the build toolchain across the project.
enrichment.impact: Provides Go runtime security fixes and performance enhancements, ensures continued compatibility with the Go ecosystem, and reduces future upgrade risk for all clusters.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix Topology Aware Hints not working when the `topology.kubernetes.io/zone` label is added after Node creation

enrichment.problem: Topology Aware Hints were ignored when the topology.kubernetes.io/zone label was added to a Node after the Node had already been created, causing pods that rely on these hints to be placed incorrectly.
enrichment.affected: Pods using Topology Aware Hints for placement, especially in clusters where the zone label is added after node creation.
enrichment.fix: The scheduler now correctly processes Topology Aware Hints even when the zone label is added post‑creation, ensuring proper pod placement based on the hints.
enrichment.impact: Pods that use Topology Aware Hints will be placed in the intended zones, improving workload distribution and reducing scheduling failures for clusters that add zone labels later.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix a data race in TopologyCache when `AddHints` and `SetNodes` are called concurrently
bugOrRegression.author: tnqn

enrichment.problem: A data race existed in the scheduler's TopologyCache when the AddHints and SetNodes methods were invoked concurrently, potentially causing incorrect cache state, panics, or wrong pod placement decisions.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using topology‑aware scheduling features (e.g., pod topology hints, topology spread constraints) that may invoke AddHints and SetNodes concurrently, affecting pod placement reliability.
enrichment.fix: Added proper synchronization to TopologyCache so that AddHints and SetNodes are mutually exclusive, ensuring thread‑safe updates and consistent topology information.
enrichment.impact: The scheduler becomes more reliable when topology hints are updated in parallel, preventing crashes or mis‑scheduling of pods that depend on topology‑aware placement.

bugOrRegression.description: Revert kubelet prober metrics `pod` tag to include actual pod name
bugOrRegression.author: a7i

enrichment.problem: Kubelet prober metrics were missing the actual pod name in the `pod` tag, making it difficult to correlate metrics with specific pods.
enrichment.affected: Users and tools that rely on kubelet prober metrics for pod‑level monitoring were seeing generic or empty pod tags.
enrichment.fix: Reverted the change so that the `pod` tag on kubelet prober metrics once again includes the real pod name.
enrichment.impact: Monitoring and alerting systems can correctly attribute probe metrics to the appropriate pods, improving observability and troubleshooting.

bugOrRegression.description:
Update kube-apiserver's priority & fairness work estimator such that 'max seats' is MIN(0.15 x nominalCL, nominalCL / handSize)
  This fixes a bug where clients with requests using hand size x max seats greater than the nominal concurrency limit can starve other requests in the same priority level.
bugOrRegression.author: andrewsykim

enrichment.problem: The apiserver's priority and fairness estimator miscomputed the maximum number of seats for a request, allowing clients whose hand size × max seats exceeded the nominal concurrency limit to monopolize capacity and starve other requests in the same priority level.
enrichment.affected: Any workload that makes high‑throughput API calls and relies on priority & fairness for request scheduling, such as large controllers or batch jobs.
enrichment.fix: The estimator now caps max seats to the smaller of 0.15 × nominalCL and nominalCL / handSize, ensuring no client can exceed the nominal concurrency limit and restoring fair request scheduling.
enrichment.impact: API callers (e.g., controllers, operators, CI pipelines) get more equitable access to the apiserver, preventing request starvation and improving latency predictability for all workloads competing at the same priority.

bugOrRegression.description: Update the Event series starting count when emitting isomorphic events from 1 to 2.
bugOrRegression.author: dgrisonnet

enrichment.problem: Event series for isomorphic events started counting from 1, leading to incorrect series identification and potential duplicate handling issues.
enrichment.affected: Clients, controllers, and test suites that consume Kubernetes events and rely on accurate event series counts.
enrichment.fix: The event emission logic was updated to start the series count at 2 when emitting isomorphic events.
enrichment.impact: Ensures correct event series numbering, improving reliability of event deduplication, monitoring, and debugging for controllers and tooling.

apiChange.description: Mark Job onPodConditions as optional in pod failure policy
apiChange.author: mimowo

enrichment.problem: The Job spec required the onPodConditions field in podFailurePolicy, forcing users to provide it even when they didn't need to specify any pod conditions.
enrichment.affected: Users creating or managing Job resources with podFailurePolicy, especially those who don't use onPodConditions.
enrichment.fix: The onPodConditions field is now marked as optional, allowing it to be omitted from a Job's podFailurePolicy.
enrichment.impact: Users can define simpler Job specifications and avoid unnecessary configuration, improving ergonomics for workloads that don't need pod condition based failure handling.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with Go 1.20.8
feature.author: cpanato

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes binaries were built with an older Go version; upgrading the Go toolchain is needed to incorporate security patches, performance improvements, and stay compatible with upstream Go releases.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes binaries (kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, controller-manager, kubelet, kube-proxy, kubectl, etc.) are rebuilt with Go 1.20.8, affecting any clusters running the new release.
enrichment.fix: All Kubernetes components are now compiled with Go 1.20.8, updating the build process and dependencies accordingly.
enrichment.impact: Ensures that the entire Kubernetes stack benefits from Go 1.20.8's security fixes and performance enhancements, reducing potential runtime issues and aligning with the Go ecosystem's supported versions.

bugOrRegression.description: Cherry-pick #115769: Fix the problem Pod terminating stuck because of trying to umount not actual mounted dir.
bugOrRegression.author: cartermckinnon

enrichment.problem: Pods could become stuck in the Terminating state because kubelet attempted to unmount a directory that was never actually mounted.
enrichment.affected: Any pod that terminates on a node where a volume mount was not successfully established could remain in Terminating state.
enrichment.fix: Kubelet now verifies that a directory is truly mounted before attempting to unmount it during pod termination, preventing the stale unmount operation.
enrichment.impact: Terminating pods now complete cleanup promptly, avoiding pod‑termination hangs and freeing node resources for new workloads.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixes a bug where images pinned by the container runtime can be garbage collected by kubelet.
bugOrRegression.author: ruiwen-zhao

enrichment.problem: Kubelet could incorrectly garbage‑collect container images that were pinned by the container runtime, leading to unexpected image removal and potential pod start failures.
enrichment.affected: All clusters where the container runtime pins images; workloads that depend on those images could be disrupted.
enrichment.fix: Kubelet now respects the image‑pinned flag from the container runtime and excludes those images from its garbage‑collection logic.
enrichment.impact: Ensures that images intentionally kept on a node remain available, preventing avoidable pod restarts or failures and improving node reliability for workloads that rely on pinned images.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixes regression in 1.25.10 causing running pods with devices to be terminated if kubelet is restarted
bugOrRegression.author: ffromani

enrichment.problem: A regression introduced in Kubernetes 1.25.10 caused the kubelet to delete running pods that were using device plugins (e.g., GPUs) whenever the kubelet was restarted.
enrichment.affected: Workloads that use device plugins (such as GPUs) were terminated when the node's kubelet was restarted.
enrichment.fix: The kubelet’s restart handling was fixed to preserve pods with allocated devices, preventing their termination during kubelet restarts.
enrichment.impact: Pods that rely on device plugins no longer experience unexpected termination after a kubelet restart, improving the reliability of workloads that use hardware accelerators and reducing downtime.

bugOrRegression.description: Ignore context canceled from validate and mutate webhook
bugOrRegression.author: divyasri537

enrichment.problem: When a validating or mutating admission webhook request is cancelled (context.Canceled), the API server treated it as an error, causing the original API request to fail even though the webhook was simply aborted.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that use validating or mutating admission webhooks; any workloads whose creation or update triggers such webhooks.
enrichment.fix: The API server now ignores context.Canceled errors from admission webhooks, treating them as non-fatal and allowing the original request to proceed based on remaining admission decisions.
enrichment.impact: Improves reliability of resources that depend on admission webhooks, preventing spurious failures during transient cancellations or client disconnects.

bugOrRegression.description: Kubeadm: fix nil pointer when etcd member is already removed
bugOrRegression.author: neolit123

enrichment.problem: kubeadm would panic with a nil pointer dereference when attempting to remove an etcd member that had already been removed.
enrichment.affected: Users running kubeadm to manage etcd members in their clusters; the issue surfaced when an etcd member had already been removed.
enrichment.fix: Added a nil check in the etcd member removal logic to safely handle already‑removed members, preventing the panic.
enrichment.impact: Stops kubeadm from crashing during etcd member cleanup, ensuring cluster lifecycle operations (init, join, upgrade) complete successfully.

other.description: When retrieving event resources, the reportingController and reportingInstance fields in the event will contain values.
other.author: HirazawaUi

enrichment.problem: When users retrieved Event objects via the API, the `reportingController` and `reportingInstance` fields were often empty, making it difficult to identify which controller or instance generated the event.
enrichment.affected: Clients or operators querying Event resources could not see reporting controller/instance information, affecting troubleshooting across all workloads.
enrichment.fix: The API server now populates `reportingController` and `reportingInstance` fields on Event resources, ensuring these values are included in the returned objects.
enrichment.impact: Improves observability and debugging of workloads by letting users see the exact controller and instance responsible for each event.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with Go 1.20.10
