enrichment.problem: Kubernetes binaries were previously built with older Go version; no direct functional problem but the build environment needed updating to incorporate security fixes and improvements from newer Go releases.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes binaries built from source are affected because they will now be compiled with Go 1.20.10.
enrichment.fix: Update the Kubernetes build process to use Go 1.20.10 for compiling all components.
enrichment.impact: All Kubernetes components (kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, kube-controller-manager, kubelet, kube-proxy, kubectl, etc.) will be compiled with the newer Go toolchain, bringing upstream Go security patches, performance enhancements, and compatibility fixes without changing runtime behavior.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with Go 1.20.9
feature.author: cpanato

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes binaries were built with older Go versions, which could miss security fixes, performance improvements, and future compatibility.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes components (kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, kube-controller-manager, kubelet, kubectl, kube-proxy) and any workloads that run the upgraded binaries.
enrichment.fix: All Kubernetes components are now compiled with Go 1.20.9, updating the Go toolchain used for the build process.
enrichment.impact: Ensures the binaries benefit from Go 1.20.9's security patches, performance enhancements, and language improvements, reducing risk of compiler‑related bugs and keeping the project on a supported Go release.

bugOrRegression.description: Adds an opt-in mitigation for http/2 DOS vulnerabilities for CVE-2023-44487 and CVE-2023-39325 for the API server when the client is unauthenticated. The mitigation may be enabled by setting the `UnauthenticatedHTTP2DOSMitigation` feature gate to `true` (it is disabled by default). An API server fronted by an L7 load balancer that already mitigates these http/2 attacks may choose not to enable the kube-apiserver mitigation to avoid disrupting load balancer → kube-apiserver connections if http/2 requests from multiple clients share the same backend connection. An API server on a private network may choose not to enable the kube-apiserver mitigation to prevent performance regressions for unauthenticated clients. Authenticated requests rely on the fix in golang.org/x/net v0.17.0 alone. https://issue.k8s.io/121197 tracks further mitigation of http/2 attacks by authenticated clients.
bugOrRegression.author: enj

enrichment.problem: Unauthenticated HTTP/2 requests to the kube-apiserver can trigger DoS vulnerabilities (CVE-2023-44487, CVE-2023-39325), allowing attackers to overload the API server.
enrichment.affected: Unauthenticated clients contacting the kube-apiserver, especially those behind L7 load balancers or on private networks.
enrichment.fix: Introduces an opt‑in feature gate `UnauthenticatedHTTP2DOSMitigation`. When enabled, the API server applies a mitigation for unauthenticated HTTP/2 traffic, limiting the impact of the vulnerabilities. Authenticated traffic is already protected by the Go net library update.
enrichment.impact: Clusters can optionally protect the API server from unauthenticated HTTP/2 DoS attacks, improving availability. Administrators can keep the mitigation disabled to avoid potential performance regression or interaction issues with external L7 load balancers.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix a bug in cronjob controller where already created jobs may be missing from the status.
bugOrRegression.author: andrewsykim

enrichment.problem: The cronjob controller could omit already created Job objects from the CronJob's .status.active list, causing the CronJob status to not reflect the true set of running jobs.
enrichment.affected: Any workloads using CronJob resources, especially those that inspect .status.active to determine running jobs.
enrichment.fix: Implemented a fix in the cronjob controller to reliably track and include all existing active Jobs in the CronJob status, ensuring the .status.active field is accurate.
enrichment.impact: Users relying on CronJob status for monitoring, debugging, or automated cleanup will now see a correct view of active jobs, preventing confusion and potential mis‑management of scheduled workloads.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed a 1.25.12 regression where kube-controller-manager can crash when StatefulSet with Parallel policy and PVC labels is scaled up.
bugOrRegression.author: aleksandra-malinowska

enrichment.problem: kube-controller-manager crashes when a StatefulSet that uses the Parallel pod management policy and has PVC labels is scaled up, a regression introduced in v1.25.12.
enrichment.affected: Clusters running StatefulSets with Parallel pod management policy and PVC labels that are scaled up; the controller‑manager process could terminate.
enrichment.fix: The controller‑manager code was corrected to handle PVC‑label‑based updates during parallel scaling without triggering a panic, restoring normal operation.
enrichment.impact: Prevents control‑plane crashes for clusters that use StatefulSets with Parallel policy and PVC labeling, ensuring reliable scaling of stateful workloads and avoiding potential downtime.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixes a bug where Services using finalizers may hold onto ClusterIP and/or NodePort allocated resources for longer than expected if the finalizer is removed using the status subresource
bugOrRegression.author: aojea

enrichment.problem: When a Service that has a finalizer is updated to remove the finalizer via the status subresource, the Service controller failed to promptly release the allocated ClusterIP and/or NodePort, causing those resources to be held longer than necessary.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that use Services with finalizers, especially when finalizers are cleared via the status subresource. Administrators could see lingering IP/port allocations.
enrichment.fix: The Service controller logic was corrected so that removal of a finalizer through the status subresource triggers immediate cleanup of the associated ClusterIP and NodePort allocations.
enrichment.impact: Prevents leak of ClusterIP and NodePort resources, avoiding exhaustion of IP or port ranges and ensuring reliable Service lifecycle handling for clusters using finalizers.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixes creationTimestamp: null causing unnecessary writes to etcd
bugOrRegression.author: alexzielenski

enrichment.problem: When an object's `metadata.creationTimestamp` was `null`, the API server treated the object as needing an update and performed a write to etcd even though the object had not changed, causing unnecessary etcd writes.
enrichment.affected: All API objects that could have a `null` `creationTimestamp`—any workload that creates or updates resources could trigger the extra write.
enrichment.fix: The API server now correctly detects a `null` `creationTimestamp` and skips the redundant write, ensuring objects are only persisted when they have actual changes.
enrichment.impact: Reduces load on etcd, improves overall control‑plane performance, and avoids needless churn in the data store, especially in clusters with high object‑creation rates.

bugOrRegression.description:
Revised the logic for DaemonSet rolling update to exclude nodes if scheduling constraints are not met.
  This eliminates the problem of rolling updates to a DaemonSet getting stuck around tolerations.
bugOrRegression.author: mochizuki875

enrichment.problem: DaemonSet rolling updates could become stuck when nodes do not satisfy scheduling constraints such as tolerations, because the update logic did not exclude those nodes.
enrichment.affected: Users running DaemonSets that rely on tolerations or other pod‑placement constraints; the DaemonSet controller could get stuck during rolling updates.
enrichment.fix: The DaemonSet rolling‑update algorithm was changed to skip nodes where the pod’s scheduling constraints (e.g., tolerations) are not met, allowing the update to proceed on eligible nodes.
enrichment.impact: Updates to DaemonSets now complete reliably even when some nodes reject the pods due to tolerations or other constraints, reducing manual intervention and preventing service disruption.

bugOrRegression.description: Sometimes, the scheduler incorrectly placed a pod in the "unschedulable" queue instead of the "backoff" queue. This happened when some plugin previously declared the pod as "unschedulable" and then in a later attempt encounters some other error. Scheduling of that pod then got delayed by up to five minutes, after which periodic flushing moved the pod back into the "active" queue.
bugOrRegression.author: pohly

enrichment.problem: The scheduler sometimes moved a pod to the "unschedulable" queue instead of the "backoff" queue when a plugin first marked it unschedulable and later encountered a different error. This caused the pod to wait up to five minutes before being retried, delaying its scheduling.
enrichment.affected: Pods that were incorrectly queued as unschedulable, leading to delayed scheduling.
enrichment.fix: Scheduler logic was corrected to ensure that when a pod already marked unschedulable encounters a subsequent error, it is placed in the backoff queue (or handled appropriately) rather than the unschedulable queue, eliminating the unintended five‑minute delay.
enrichment.impact: Pods are scheduled more promptly, reducing unnecessary latency and improving overall cluster responsiveness, especially for workloads that rely on scheduler plugins which may encounter multiple scheduling errors.

other.description: Etcd: update to v3.5.9
other.author: nikhita

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes bundled an older etcd version (pre‑v3.5.9) which contains known bugs and security vulnerabilities.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that run the default Kubernetes version with the older embedded etcd (e.g., kubeadm‑created clusters) were vulnerable to the bugs and CVEs addressed in etcd v3.5.9.
enrichment.fix: The release updates the embedded etcd dependency to v3.5.9, bringing in upstream bug fixes and security patches.
enrichment.impact: Clusters using the default Kubernetes distribution gain improved stability and security for the data store, reducing risk of data corruption or unauthorized access.

other.description: Fixes an issue where the vsphere cloud provider will not trust a certificate if:

enrichment.problem: The vSphere cloud provider refused to trust a TLS certificate under certain conditions, causing connectivity failures to the vSphere API.
enrichment.affected: Kubernetes clusters that use the vSphere cloud provider, especially those with custom or self‑signed vSphere API certificates.
enrichment.fix: Updated the vSphere cloud provider to correctly validate and trust the provided certificate, allowing secure communication with vSphere endpoints.
enrichment.impact: Clusters that use the vSphere cloud provider with custom or self‑signed certificates can now connect to vSphere without errors, restoring volume provisioning and other cloud‑provider features.

other.description: The issuer of the certificate is unknown (x509.UnknownAuthorityError)

enrichment.problem: TLS connections fail because the certificate's issuer cannot be verified, resulting in an x509.UnknownAuthorityError during authentication.
enrichment.affected: Kubernetes control plane and node components that perform TLS authentication, such as the API server, kubelet, controller manager, and scheduler, could be unable to communicate.
enrichment.fix: The update adds proper handling of the certificate authority chain and ensures the relevant CA bundles are loaded, allowing the issuer to be recognized and the TLS handshake to succeed.
enrichment.impact: Components that rely on mutual TLS (e.g., kube-apiserver, kubelet, controller-manager, scheduler) may reject connections, leading to authentication failures and potential cluster downtime.

other.description: The requested name does not match the set of authorized names (x509.HostnameError)

enrichment.problem: When a client presented a TLS certificate, the server rejected the request because the certificate's hostname did not match any of the authorized names, resulting in an x509.HostnameError.
enrichment.affected: Any component that performs TLS client‑certificate authentication, particularly the kube-apiserver handling incoming requests.
enrichment.fix: The hostname verification logic was corrected so that the set of authorized names is properly evaluated, allowing certificates with valid hostnames to be accepted.
enrichment.impact: Clients that rely on client certificate authentication (e.g., kubelet, custom tools, CI pipelines) can now successfully connect without manual work‑arounds, reducing authentication failures.

other.description: The error surfaced after attempting a connection contains one of the substrings: "certificate is not trusted" or "certificate signed by unknown authority"
other.author: MadhavJivrajani

enrichment.problem: Connections to a component failed with vague errors when the TLS handshake encountered certificates that were not trusted or signed by an unknown authority, making it hard to diagnose and causing connection drops.
enrichment.affected: Clusters where kube‑controller‑manager/cloud‑controller‑manager or kubelet connects to an API server or external cloud provider endpoint using a certificate that is not trusted (e.g., self‑signed certs).
enrichment.fix: The code now correctly detects these TLS errors, surfaces a clear error message, and handles the failure path properly, preventing silent connection failures.
enrichment.impact: Users and cloud‑provider integrations can now reliably detect and troubleshoot certificate trust issues, reducing downtime in clusters that use custom or self‑signed certificates.

other.description: Set the resolution for the job_controller_job_sync_duration_seconds metric from 4ms to 1min
other.author: mimowo

enrichment.problem: The job_controller_job_sync_duration_seconds metric recorded data at a 4ms resolution, leading to very high cardinality and excessive storage/processing overhead for monitoring systems.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that scrape the job_controller_job_sync_duration_seconds metric, especially users relying on fine‑grained Job controller latency data.
enrichment.fix: The metric's resolution was changed to 1 minute, coarsening the data granularity and drastically reducing the number of samples generated.
enrichment.impact: Reduces metric cardinality and storage requirements, improves performance of the metrics pipeline, and makes monitoring the Job controller more practical for clusters of any size.

securityFixes.title: Insufficient input sanitization in in-tree storage plugin leads to privilege escalation on Windows nodes
securityFixes.description: A security issue was discovered in Kubernetes where a user that can create pods and persistent volumes on Windows nodes may be able to escalate to admin privileges on those nodes. Kubernetes clusters are only affected if they are using an in-tree storage plugin for Windows nodes.
